On the chat page your conversations are listed beside the channels, so while that page is in front of you it also asks for that list, at most every half minute and sooner when somebody new has written; which conversation you pick there is kept nowhere, not even in the page’s address. What is kept. Whether you take messages, and who you blocked. For each conversation: the two usernames, which of you asked, whether it was accepted, and its messages, each its words, its picture and description if it has one, the sticker if it is one (a copy of one of your avatars, chimeras, pets or patches, or your battle jacket, taken when you sent it), who reacted to it with what, who sent it, BASE if a moderator did, and when it was sent and last edited. An empty marker for each of you, with when it was written, so your list can be found without anybody keeping a list of who talks to whom. Nothing about who read what, for anybody else: no read receipts, nothing telling the other person a message was seen, nothing saying somebody is typing, and nothing is counted: no number of unread messages anywhere. For yourself, when you last read each conversation is kept so the radio can mark what is new to you; see what is new to you. Deleting them. Forget me and Delete my account under Account delete your switch, your block list and every conversation you are in, for both of you. Reports stay on the desk for their thirty days. What we do not keep. The same as the radio: no IP address, nothing in any log, no copy anywhere, and no list of who has written to whom. Every answer about messages asks search engines not to index or archive it. We keep messages because the two of you wrote them to each other, and keeping them for two weeks is what a conversation takes. Accepting a conversation is your consent to it, and Block, Forget me and deleting your username take it back.

A chimera is one creature you made out of two animals in Chimera Obscura. Making one, changing it and naming it happen in your browser and send nothing: a link to it carries it after the # in the address, which never reaches any server. Chimeras are the sixth thing the street can keep under a person, after pets, avatars, jobs, patches and profile cards, and only when you press Keep it in my Profile. That was Ryan’s call, 2026-10-18. A chimera is a list of choices, never a picture. What is kept is which animal gave each part, every one a word out of the room’s own shelf, which our server checks against that shelf and refuses anything else; and its name, if you give it one. Nothing about when you made it is kept. The drawing is made fresh from the choices wherever it is shown. Keeping one. Signed on to the CB, Keep it in my Profile in the room sends your pass, the choices and the name. Renaming or deleting one from Profile sends your pass, which chimera and what changed. We keep up to 24 at once. Where they are kept. Under a scrambled form of your handle, the same as your pets and your avatars, so the store does not list handles, at Netlify, beside the channel. Only your password reaches them: nobody else can sign on as your username. Showing them, if you choose to. With a claimed username, Show my chimeras on the CB in Profile shows them in your profile, with their names, to anybody signed on to the CB who opens it. It is off until you switch it on. We keep only that it is on, and when you switched it on; switching it off, Forget me and deleting your username delete that. Opening somebody’s profile sends your pass and their handle, and we keep neither; the answer never says whether somebody has chimeras they have not shown. As a sticker. Sticker on the radio can send one of your chimeras to the channel you are tuned to, with its name and which animal gave which part. It is a message like any other, kept and deleted with the channel’s messages. Deleting them. Delete any one from Profile, which asks once more; Forget me under Account deletes them all with your pets, and whether they are shown; and Delete my account deletes them with your username. What we do not keep. The same as the radio: no IP address, nothing in any log, and no list of who has a chimera or who looked at one. Every answer about your chimeras asks search engines not to index or archive it. We keep your chimeras because you pressed Keep and asked the street to remember them, and keeping them is what that takes. Pressing Keep is your consent to it, and deleting them takes it back.

The MUD Room has a world out its back door called the Slake, a multi-user dungeon with nobody to fight. Playing it on your own happens inside the page and sends nothing. Meeting other people on it is part of the CB and runs on the radio’s rules, with one switch of its own, Be seen out here, which is off every time you arrive and is never remembered. What it sends, and when. Only once you are signed on to the CB and have pressed Be seen out here, and only while the tab is in front of you. Then, every few seconds and whenever you move, it sends your pass, which place you are in, and a random number the page makes up for this visit, which nobody else is ever shown and which is how your visit moves and leaves without a list of visits anywhere. When you say something, your words come too. Switch it off, put the tab behind another or leave the page, and it tells us you have gone and sends nothing more. Who can see you. Anybody else who is signed on, has chosen to be seen, and is in the same place as you, by your handle. Being seen is also the only way to see: nobody can watch the Slake without being seen on it. Nobody is given a list of who is out there, or a number of people, and the map shows only you. A username says whoever holds its password is there, and nothing more about who they are. What we keep. While you are seen, one record: your handle, whether you signed on as the base station, which place you are in, the time of your last check, and the visit’s random number. Moving replaces it rather than adding to it, so where you have been is not kept. It is shown to nobody thirty seconds after your last check, and deleted when you stop being seen or leave, or within two minutes by anybody else’s check, or by the hourly sweep at the latest. What is said in a place is kept like the radio’s channel: the latest hundred things said there, each with its handle, its words and its time, each deleted two weeks after it was said, unless our administrators set every channel otherwise, and the base station can take one off sooner. There is no archive, no backup and no copy. What we do not keep. The same as the radio: no IP address, nothing in any log, no list of who was out there, and no record of where anybody went. Your tide, what you are carrying, the places you have found and the map stay in your page and are gone when you close it. Where it is kept. Beside the channel, at Netlify, under Netlify’s privacy policy. We keep that you are in a place because you chose to be seen there, and keeping it for as long as you are is what that takes. Pressing Be seen out here is your consent to it, and pressing it again takes that back. We keep what you say in a place for two weeks because you said it to whoever is there, the same as on the radio, and you can ask us to delete it sooner.

A few rooms have boxes you can type into, and none of them sends anything. The Guild’s hand-in box checks a code inside the page, and sends which job to us only once you have switched on keeping your jobs in your Profile. The Zibaldone’s attribution slip puts a block of text on your own clipboard, and you decide where it goes. The Foundry sets the words you type in a typeface, in your browser. The MUD Room’s command line plays the game inside the page and sends nothing, except what you say while you are seen on the Slake. The CB is the one exception: its boxes, the chalkboard’s, the pebble bowls’, the suggestion box’s, the fence’s on Pando Calrissian’s hill, the Fridge of Sighs’ and what you say on the Slake included, send what you type, to us, as written up above.

Because we hold so little, most of what the law gives you a right to ask about is not here to ask about. What there is: Your photograph, your recording or your name in a credit: ask us to see it, correct it or take it down, and we will. What you said on the CB: ask us and we will delete it now rather than at its two weeks. After that there is nothing left to ask about. What you said on the Slake: ask us and we will delete it now rather than at its two weeks. Where you were is already gone. What you chalked on the board: ask us and we will rub it out now rather than at the end of its week. What you pinned on Pando Calrissian’s fence: ask us and we will take it down now rather than at the end of its week. Your waterings are not there to ask about: the tree never knew they were yours. What you dropped in the suggestion box: take it down yourself, from the box, or ask any moderator and they will. Your pets: Forget me under Account on your radio deletes them, with your avatars, at once, or ask us and we will. Your avatars: delete any one from Profile, or Forget me there deletes them all at once, and the one you wore comes off Who’s online first. Your chimeras: delete any one from Profile, or Forget me there deletes them all at once. The jobs kept in your Profile: switch off Keep my jobs in my Profile on the Guild’s board, or Forget me under Account deletes them with everything else. Your battle jacket: Forget me under Account takes every patch off it, or ask us and we will. Your crystal pouch: put any crystal back from Profile, or Forget me under Account empties it, or ask us and we will. Your herb basket: put any herb back from Profile, or Forget me under Account empties it, or ask us and we will. Your props: take any one off your Props tab, or Forget me under Account deletes them all with everything waiting for you. A prop you wrote for somebody else: take it back from their tab, or ask a moderator and they will take it down. Your username: Delete my account under Account deletes it, its password, your pets, your avatars, your chimeras, your jobs, your patches, your crystals, your herbs, your profile card, your props and your chat status at once. Ask a moderator if you cannot get in, and they can delete it for you. An animal’s name in a shelter or on the list of everybody adopted: tell us which animal and we will take the name off. Nothing says which ones were yours, so only you can tell us. A word on the Fridge of Sighs: nothing says which words were yours, so we cannot find them for you; but if a word or a sentence should not be there, tell us what it says and we will take it down. Our host’s logs: Netlify holds those. Ask us and we will ask on your behalf, or contact Netlify directly. What your browser keeps: it is on your device and yours to clear. We never keep a copy, the CB pass included. If you are in the EU or the UK, you also have the right to access, correct, erase, restrict, object to and move your personal data, and to complain to your data protection authority. We do not sell or share personal information for advertising, so a Global Privacy Control signal from your browser has nothing here to opt you out of — the answer is already no.
If you have found a hole in this site, report it privately on GitHub; the policy is in SECURITY.md and security.txt. A report there is handled by GitHub under GitHub’s privacy statement.

If what this site does with your information changes, this page changes first, the date at the top moves, and the change is written up in the changelog on the day, where the feed will pick it up. HOW LOUD DO YOU WANT IT? Starts wherever your device says. Nothing moves, flashes, or plays until you say so.

The CB is the street’s radio: a chat channel patterned after citizens band radio, in a panel in the corner of every page. This guide goes through it part by part, top to bottom, with every button named the way the radio names it. To get on, go to the front desk at the Community Center; the house norms are there too, and Privacy says what the CB keeps. Last updated 2026-10-18.

Open is on, folded is off. Open, with the tab in front of you, the radio listens every four seconds. Folded, or behind another tab, it sends nothing. A hundred messages a channel, each gone two weeks after it was sent, unless our administrators set a channel otherwise, so people in every timezone can read what was said while they slept. Once a channel is full, the newest pushes the oldest off. In this channel says what the one you are on keeps. A message from before today says which day, yesterday or the day’s name, beside its time. Notifications only if you ask. The radio has no chime and never a number of anything, and the tab’s title never changes. With a claimed username, what is new to you is marked with a dot, and listed under Unreads. Notifications, under Your radio, can tell a device about mentions, rooms you follow, calls starting and everything on World, even with the site closed. Names, never numbers. A reaction says who pressed it, and Who’s online says who is around and where, and which rooms have somebody in their call. Nothing shows a count. Nothing on it moves when a message arrives, and it is the same radio in every room. The one thing that ever moves is a theme’s drawing, and only at MAX GLITTER or when you let it.

The radio sits in the bottom right corner of every page. Two places do not have it. The Healing Checkpoint and Stay Frosty each promise something the radio would break, so it waits outside their doors. The private rooms off the Town Hall show it only to the moderators each room is for, and Tasks and the Office only to our directors, board members and administrators, the people who can open them. The Community Center has its own front desk instead of the bar, and once you sign on there the radio appears in the corner.
Before you sign on: the guest bar

Until you sign on, the corner holds a smaller bar. It is not the radio. It knows nothing about the channel and sends nothing to it, and the only thing it remembers is whether you left it open. Control What it does CB The radio’s name. Teleport Opens the teleporter, the same one the radio has. Get on the CB Opens a panel saying what the CB is and how to join it with an invite, with a form to sign on. It reads Fold away while the panel is open. Your username The name you go by on the channel, which you chose when you joined. Your password Your own password, which you chose when you joined. Sign on Checks the password and swaps this bar for the radio, on every page, until you sign off. A moderator whose username is not claimed yet is sent to the joining page instead. The front desk at the Community Center has the same form, and more under Forgotten your password?: Email me a reset code, which takes Your username and The email address on it and sends a code from our team’s mailbox, if that is the address on the username; and a form taking Your username, Your recovery code, a reset code we emailed, or a moderator’s, A new password and The same again, then Set it and sign on.

The joining page is where an invite becomes a username. An invite’s link opens it with Your invite code filled in, and the page says whether the invite works. Type A username, and it says whether the name is free; a moderator’s username asks for The moderators’ password as well, and needs no invite. Then A password of your own, eight characters or more, The same again, and, if recovery by email is switched on, An email address for password recovery, if you want one (optional). Join claims the username, shows your recovery code once, and I have kept it brings the radio. On with the old starter password, or the moderators’? The radio does not open. In its place is Claim and your username, with A password of your own, eight characters or more, The same again and an email address if you want one, and Sign off. Claim, keep the recovery code, press I have kept it, and the radio comes. Added to a Home Screen or a Dock, the street starts afresh. On an iPhone or iPad, stimpunks.world added to the Home Screen, and on a Mac, added to the Dock from Safari, keeps what it remembers apart from Safari’s, so you sign on to the CB again there, and anything else the street keeps in your browser, like the dial’s setting and the animals you rescued, starts again there too. The dial starts at Gentle if your device asks for less motion. Installed from Chrome or Edge, it shares what the browser remembers, so you stay signed on.

Signed on, the bar runs along the top of the radio. You can drag the radio by any part of the bar that is not a button. Control What it does When folded CB The radio’s name, and somewhere to drag it by. shown Teleport Opens the teleporter under the bar. hidden Move, the six dots Drag the dots, or any part of the bar that is not a button, to put the radio somewhere else. Or press the dots: they take the keyboard and say how it works, and then the arrow keys move the radio 24 pixels a press and Home puts it back in the corner. The radio remembers where you left it. Not at Full, which fills the window and has nowhere to move to. shown − and + Smaller and larger: one press goes from Full to Large to Normal to Small to an icon, or back up. Each says which size it goes to, and says so when the radio is already as small or as large as it goes. hidden Fold away Folds the radio down to its bar and stops it. It reads Switch on while folded, and that opens it again. reads Switch on

State What you see Is it listening? Icon Only an icon of a CB set, the aerial, the readout and the handset, on the radio’s own case. Press it, or press Enter on it, to open the radio at Small; drag it to put it somewhere else. Nothing on it changes when a message comes in. Good for getting the radio right out of the way while you host or follow a film. yes, so a film you host or follow carries on and Be seen here still holds. A screen reader hears nothing new at this size; Speak new messages aloud still speaks. Choose Small to keep an ear on the channel. Small The bar, the line saying what you are tuned to, and only the newest message. Good for keeping the radio on over a film. yes, and it still reads new messages to a screen reader Normal Everything, in a narrow panel. yes Large Everything, wider and taller, for long messages and pictures. yes Full The whole window, for when you want only the CB, with the channel as tall as the window. On a wide window the parts stand in three columns, in the order they come everywhere else: Where you are and the channel on the left, wide; then Messages, In this channel, Who’s around, Unreads and Events; then the rest. A room’s call window stays on top of it. yes Folded Only CB, Move and Switch on. no. It sends nothing, stops reading aloud, stops hosting and following a film, and stops you being seen. The radio is never wider or taller than your window. If it would cover the button it has just got ready for you to press, it goes Small for the moment and says so; + makes it larger again.

Under the bar the radio is in parts, top to bottom, each under a heading lettered on the case, with a groove in the case between one part and the next. A screen reader can move between the headings. Small shows none of them. At Full on a wide window they stand in columns instead, left to right in the same order, and each column scrolls by itself. Heading What is under it Where you are The name of the room you are in, in the largest words on the radio, I need a bodymind break, the Glitter dial and Open in Chat. Channel World or this room, Follow this room, links to the forums and to the World room, which lists the rooms active now and the calls going, the messages, and the box to write in. Messages Your messages: writing to one other person. In this channel On the channel as and your handle, then a heading for each of its smaller parts: Seen here, with Be seen here and who else is seen; In this room’s call, with Join this room’s call and who is in it; Your familiar, with Bring my familiar; and On now, what is on now in the room. A heading with nothing under it just now is not shown. The chat page has a part of the same name. Who’s around Who’s online, Join World call, Show the call window while a call is in a window of its own, and Your chat status. Unreads World, the rooms you follow and your conversations, while something new has been said in them, for a claimed username. Events Events, the list of what is scheduled on World and in the rooms you can go into, with Schedule an event. Watching together Hosting now, everybody hosting a film on the street, with Catch up and Follow beside a host in your room, then Add my spot, Host this film and Screen a video, and the radio’s answers to all of them. The part is only there while one of them is. You Profile and Account, whose trays open under this heading, Your page, and Sign off. Your radio The switches for a screen reader and for speaking aloud, Themes, Notifications and Pop out, and links to the house norms and this guide.
Where you are, and In this channel

At the top of the radio, under Where you are, is the name of the room this page is, as the street names it, in the largest words on the radio: The Den, say, or The Street on the front page. It is where you are standing, which is not always the channel you are hearing: tuned to World, you hear the whole street from wherever you are. A page that is not a room says A page that is not a room on the street. The channel comes straight after it, then Messages, then In this channel (Ryan’s order, 2026-10-23, as the chat page has it): a line saying On the channel as and your handle, then smaller parts, each under a heading of its own: Seen here, with Be seen here and who else is seen here; In this room’s call, with Join this room’s call in a room when calls are switched on, and who is in the call; Your familiar, with Bring my familiar when a familiar is following you, or where to find one; and On now, what is on now in the room. A heading with nothing under it just now is not shown.

Under Where you are, I need a bodymind break opens a calm screen over the page: a far treeline in mist, a few words, and nothing else unless you ask for it. Folded, the radio has a Break on its bar instead, and so does the CB bar for anybody not signed on; the How loud do you want it? box at the top of a page has the same button. On the break are links to crisis lines and warmlines and to our Help page, for when a break is not enough, three quiet rooms on the street, and a forest or Monterey Bay Aquarium’s jellies to watch if you like: the forest says how long it runs, the jellies are live and run until you close them, and neither fetches anything from YouTube until you press it. If something on the page is playing, the break offers to pause it, and pauses nothing by itself. Nothing on it moves, at any setting, and while it is up the radio reads nothing aloud; what was said meanwhile is on the channel when you come back. I’m back, or Escape, closes it. It keeps nothing and sends nothing (the privacy page). Helen Edgar’s idea, after Cavendish Space’s button of the same name.

Beside I need a bodymind break, Glitter dial opens the dial from the top of a page on the radio itself, so you can turn it from any page the radio is on, the pages with no dial of their own included. Under How loud do you want it? are Gentle, Regular and MAX GLITTER; under Feeling overwhelmed? Escape to a low-stimulation mode. are Warm Light, Cool Dark, Plant Green and Red Light, and while one is on, Back to the rooms’ own colours. The level and the mode that are on are filled in, and a line under them says what the setting does, in the dial’s own words. It is the same dial as the one on the page, not a second one: turn either and the other follows, and your browser keeps your setting as it always has (the privacy page). From the radio’s own window, it turns the page you came from, and the window with it. Pressed again, Glitter dial folds it away. To keep the room as it is and quieten only the radio, the same four modes are themes too, under Low stimulation.

After the Glitter dial, Open in Chat takes you to the chat page with the room you are in picked, so the room’s channel is in the middle and every other channel is down the left. On a page that is not a room it opens on World. It is not on the chat page itself, and not in a room that keeps to itself, which the chat page does not list. While you are in a call it opens in a new tab, as every link on the radio does, so the call stays up.
What is new to you: Unreads

With a claimed username, the radio marks what has been said since you last read it, with a dot and, to a screen reader, the words something new. It is a mark, never a number, and nothing about it sounds, moves or flashes. Where the dots are. On World and This room when the channel you are not tuned to has something new; on Your messages and on a conversation in it when the other person has written since you read it, a first message to you included. Unreads, the part under Who’s around (on the chat page, above the channels), lists them: World, the rooms you follow, and your conversations. Press one to go there: World tunes to World, a room on this page tunes to it, another room is a link to it, and a conversation opens under Messages. Follow this room: off, beside This room under Channel, puts the room you are in on Unreads whenever something new is said there. Which rooms you follow is kept in this browser only. Follow every room: off, at the foot of Unreads, follows every room you can go into at once, the rooms added later and the forums’ categories you can read included, instead of one at a time (Norah’s ask, 2026-10-21). While it is on, Follow this room is not shown, because this room is followed already. Switched off, Unreads goes back to the rooms you followed one by one, which it leaves as they were. A room that keeps to itself is never on it, and it is kept in this browser only. To be notified about every room as well, Notifications has a Follow every room of its own. What counts as read. A channel when its newest message is on your screen at the foot of the log, with the radio open; a conversation when you have it open. Reading on one device clears the dot on your others, because the street keeps, for your username, when you last read each one, and nothing else. See the privacy page. The radio asks what is new at most every half a minute, and only while it is open, so a dot can take that long to come.

In a room, Be seen here: off, under In this channel, says whether it is on, as the switches under Your radio do; pressed, it says Be seen here: on and puts you, by your handle, on Who’s online for anybody signed on, with the room you are in, and shows you and anybody else who has switched it on in the same room to each other. In a room that keeps to itself it shows you only to people seen there. While it is off you are on nobody’s list; you can still open Who’s online, but not see who else is in this room or in its call. Also seen here: lists the others, alphabetically, by handle. Nobody else here is seen. means just that. In this room’s call: lists everybody in the room’s call, so you can see who is there before you join. Names only, and never a count. The lines update quietly, without announcing themselves. Your browser remembers the switch. Folding the radio, leaving the page or putting the tab behind another takes you out of sight. With a familiar following you (a chimera you took with you from Chimera Obscura or from Profile) and a claimed username, Bring my familiar: off comes under Be seen here; with no familiar following you, a line there says where to take one from. Pressed, it says Bring my familiar: on, and the people seen in the same room as you see your familiar there, walking about the room, with its name and its sayings, while you are seen; you see theirs, and pressing one says whose it is. It is never on Who’s online. Taking a different chimera with you changes what they see, and sending yours home takes it back in. The privacy page says what is kept.

Who’s online opens two lists. While it is open they are redrawn every few seconds, quietly, and neither shows a number. Left open, it is open again on the next page, until you close it. Beside it, Join World call opens the World call. People: everybody who has switched on Be seen here, in alphabetical order, with BASE beside a moderator’s name the way the channel marks it, their chat status, if they chose one, the avatar each person wears, if it wears one, and the room each is in, with the nameplate they chose, if they chose one, as a strip under the line. A screen reader hears an avatar as what its owner wrote about it, or not at all, and the nameplate not at all. A name opens that person’s profile, the same as pressing a handle on the channel, and a room’s name takes you there. Your own line says (you), and a line under the list says whether you are on it. Calls going now: the World call, while somebody is in it, then every room whose call has somebody in it, in walking order, and a room’s name takes you there. It names the room and nothing else. Who is in a call is shown in its room, to anybody seen there. This list appears once 8x8 is telling us who is in calls. A room that keeps to itself is never on either list, and a room the base keeps is named only to the people it is for.

Be seen here says you are in a room. Your chat status, at the foot of Who’s around, says whether you would like to be talked to, wherever you are, because somebody can be about and still not be chatty (Ryan’s ask, 2026-10-24). It is one of the interaction badges, in the words and shapes of the Cavendish Space Project’s interaction cards, after the colour communication badges Autism Network International started at the first Autreat: come say hi, a green circle: “i want to talk — you can start.” Saying hello first is welcome. people i know, a yellow triangle: “only say hi if we’ve met.” If you have not met, let them say hello first. not right now, a red square: “please don’t start talking to me.” Hold back, and do not take it personally. Each badge is its shape and its words as well as its colour, so nobody has to tell colours apart to read one, and it looks the same in every theme. Choose with the radio buttons, and half a second after you stop it is kept and the radio says so; none shows nothing. Where people see it. Beside your name on Who’s online and on Also seen here in the same room, on your profile under your name, and at the top of a conversation with you under Messages, before anybody writes, with what the badge asks. It is a sign, not a lock. It stops nobody writing to you, and somebody showing yellow or red can still start a conversation themselves, and be answered. It starts as none and stays as you left it. Nothing chooses one for you, and nothing changes it but you: it never goes to idle or away when you stop typing, and it never runs out. It is the same on every device you sign on with. Why not Discord’s Online, Idle, Do Not Disturb and Invisible. Online and Invisible are Be seen here, a room at a time. Idle is worked out from when somebody stopped touching their keyboard, and telling everybody that is not ours to do; the radio stops listening anyway when it is folded or behind another tab, and you drop off Who’s online half a minute later. Do Not Disturb tells people to leave you be, which not right now says better, and holds your notifications, which Notifications does device by device. The privacy page says what is kept: which badge, and nothing about when.

Under Channel, two buttons choose what you hear: Control What it does World The channel the whole street shares. A new radio starts here, and tuned to World the radio never says which room you are in. This room The channel of the room you are standing in. Walk into another room and you hear that room’s channel instead. Pages that are not rooms do not have one. In the World room the room’s own channel is World, so there the button is not shown and the radio says Tuned to World, which is this room’s own channel. In the forums, this room is the category you are reading, below. A line above the messages says Tuned to World or Tuned to the room’s name. Unless our administrators set a channel otherwise, it keeps its latest 100 messages, each for two weeks, and the first line under In this channel says what this one keeps. A quiet one says Nobody has said anything in the last two weeks. The radio shows the latest hundred messages; Earlier messages, above them, shows a hundred more each time, as far back as the channel keeps.

Each message starts with a line: the sender’s handle, a mark if it has one, and the time it was sent, by your clock. Then come its words, a picture or sticker if it has one, and its reactions. A reply has a line above all that, saying whose message it answers. At the end of the line are three small buttons, React (a smiley with a plus), Reply (a curved arrow) and More (three dots). They show while your pointer is on the message or the keyboard is anywhere in it, and they are always there on a phone or tablet. Out of sight they are still in their place, so Tab reaches them and a screen reader names them. Part What it means or does The handle A button. Press it to open that person’s profile over the page: their card, and their avatars, pets, badges and jobs, battle jacket, chimeras and props, as they have chosen to show them. A name on Who’s online opens the same profile. BASE Sent by one of our moderators. Only the server can put this mark there. Every username signs on only with its owner’s own password, so every name on the channel is somebody’s. BOT Said by The Feed or The Source on its own channel: something new on one of The Feed’s boards, or a new commit on one of The Source’s terraces, with its site, its name as a link and, for a commit, its short id, its day and whose hands made it. Its name opens no profile, nobody can edit it, and only a moderator can take it off; React and Reply work as on any message. Follow the room by name to be told about each one. See the privacy page. edited and a time Its sender has changed its words since they sent it, and when they last did. The words it had before are not kept anywhere. React, the smiley Opens the reactions under the message. Reply, the curved arrow Answers this message: see replies. Replying to and a name Above the line of a reply: whose message it answers, and the start of its words. Press it to go to that message, which gets an amber edge. Once that message has gone off the air, it says so instead. More, the three dots Opens Copy, Read aloud, Edit, Take to the forums and Take off in a row under the message’s line, whichever this message has. Press it again, or Escape, to fold them away. Where your device has no voice, a message with no words that is not yours has no More. Copy, under More Puts the message’s words on your own clipboard, as they were typed. It reads Copied for a moment. Read aloud, under More Reads that one message out now, in the same voice as Speak new messages aloud, whether that is on or off: the handle, whose message it replies to, the words, and what its picture or sticker is. It stops whatever the radio was saying first, and reads Stop reading while it reads; press it again to stop. Only a voice built into your own device, and the burst of static round it goes at the Gentle setting. Edit, under More Only on messages you sent, and a moderator’s only on their own. Opens the words in a box where they were: Enter or Save saves, Shift and Enter starts a new line (on a phone, Return starts a new line and Save saves), and Escape or Cancel leaves it as it was. Only the words change: its picture, sticker and reactions stay, and it still goes two weeks after you first sent it. ↑ in an empty message box edits your newest message. A message marked BASE edits only for the base. Take to the forums, under More With a claimed username, on a message with words in it. Opens a box under the readout listing what is on the channel now, with this message ticked: tick any others, then Start a topic with these opens the forums with them, copied exactly as they were sent. Ask everybody in the conversation first. Not in a room that keeps to itself. Take off, under More Only on messages you sent. Takes the message off the air for everybody, with its picture, sticker and reactions, and puts the keyboard back in the message box. It cannot be put back. A message marked BASE comes off only for the base. A picture Press it to see it larger, with Download and Close. Download under it keeps a copy on your device. A sticker A drawing of one of the sender’s avatars, pets or patches, or of their whole battle jacket, with its words under it. It goes when its message goes. Links in a message. An address on this street is an ordinary link. An address on another site, written with https://, opens in a new tab and has an arrow and the site’s name after it, like ↗ example.com, so you can see where it goes before you press it. A room written as #the-den shows as #The Den, linked: on the chat page to its channel there, and anywhere else to the room. A room written as /the-den, after a space or at the start of a line, shows as /The Den and always goes to the room’s page; and/or and /usr/bin stay words. A time like @34:12 is a button that moves your own film to that place: see watching together. Link cards. An address on another site, on its own in a message, gets a card under the message a moment after it goes out, up to three in a message: the site’s name, who made it, a title that is a link saying where it goes, and the page’s description or, for a post on X, Bluesky and the like, the words of the post. A YouTube or Vimeo video plays in the card: its button says the title, and how long it runs when that could be found out (otherwise the player shows it as soon as it starts), and nothing from YouTube or Vimeo loads until you press it. A video that cannot play on other sites is a link to watch it there instead. A card never has a picture in it, and nothing else plays in one. To send a link without a card, write it in angle brackets, <https://example.com>; a link with your own words on it, [words](address), and a link to a room on the street get none either. A video playing in a card is not one Host this film or Follow can see. At Small the cards are put away. What our server reads to make a card is on the privacy page. It never scrolls under you. If you have scrolled up to read, new messages wait at the bottom. The radio follows them only when you were already at the bottom, or when you have just transmitted.

Reply, the curved arrow on a message’s line, opens a line above the message box, Replying to their name and the start of their words, and puts the keyboard in the box. Write and transmit as usual, and your message goes out as an answer to theirs, with that line above it on everybody’s radio. Cancel reply, or Escape in the box, lets the reply go and keeps what you wrote. A reply keeps nothing of the message it answers but which one it was. The line above it is drawn from what is on the channel now, so if its sender edits it the line changes, and if it is taken off or its two weeks are up, the line says it answered a message no longer on the channel. If the message you are answering goes while you are writing, the radio says so and what you write goes out on its own. Somebody is told you replied only if they switched on When somebody replies to me.

React, the smiley, opens a row of quick reactions: a heart, thumbs up, laughing, a party, eyes, sparkles, a penguin for a pebble, a dog, a cat, an otter, a rainbow, a unicorn, the sign of the horns, a hedgehog, a hugging face, people hugging, a crying face, and a hundred points. Under them, Or any emoji takes one emoji of your own from your system’s emoji picker (Control, Command and Space on a Mac, the emoji key on a phone, Windows and . on Windows), and its own React button sends it. Under the message, each reaction shows the handles of everybody who pressed it, alphabetically, and never a number. Press a reaction there to add yours, or to take yours back.

Control What it does Your message The box. Up to 2,000 characters, and it keeps your lines. It grows as you type, and you can drag its corner to make it taller. Picture Adds a screenshot or a photo. You can also paste one into the box, with Ctrl or Cmd and V. See pictures. Sticker Shows your avatars, then your chimeras, then your pets, then your battle jacket and each patch on it. Press one to send a sticker of it to the channel straight away; what is in the box stays there. No avatars yet? Draw one at the Bodymind Booth. No chimeras? Make one in Chimera Obscura. No pets yet? Adopt one at Rescue A Cat or Rescue A Dog. Transmit Sends the message, with its picture if it has one. Keys in the box What they do Enter Transmits, unless the list of rooms or people is open. On a phone or a tablet, where there is no Shift and Enter, Return starts a new line instead and Transmit sends, and the box starts four lines tall. Shift and Enter Starts a new line. Ctrl or Cmd and Enter Transmits, on any device, for a tablet with a keyboard on it. ↑, with the box empty Edits your newest message on the channel. See Edit. # and the start of a room’s name Opens a list of rooms. ↑ and ↓ move through it, Enter or Tab picks one, and Escape leaves your # as you typed it. / and the start of a room’s name Opens the same list for the rooms’ pages, after a space or at the start of a line, and puts /the-den in, which links to the room itself rather than its channel. @ and the start of somebody’s handle Opens a list of people to mention, and the roles you can call, the same way: ↑ and ↓ move, Enter or Tab puts their handle in, and Escape leaves your @ as you typed it. A place in a film, @34:12, opens nothing. Answers from the radio, like Transmitting… or No signal. That did not go out., appear in one line just above the box. If you send more than twelve messages in a minute it asks you to wait a moment.

A little Markdown works, and the radio builds it into the page as text, never as code. Type You get **bold** bold *italic* or _italic_ italic. A single _ inside a word, as in snake_case, stays as typed. ~~struck~~ struck through `code` code, with nothing inside it changed Three backticks on a line of their own, before and after a block of code > at the start of a line a quote -, * or 1. at the start of a line a list # and a space at the start of a line a heading, and ## or ### a smaller one. With no space, #the-den is still a room. [words](an address) a link with your words on it. One to another site still says where it goes after your words, as ↗ the site, so no words can make it look like a link on the street. Words that are themselves an address, like [paypal.com](…), are not made a link unless the link goes to that same site: otherwise it stays as typed, and its address is a link of its own. So [Chat — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/chat) is a link. [[ and part of a name a link to a forum topic, or for our directors, board members and administrators to a task, a grant request, a case or a contact: pick it from the list that opens. Everybody who can open it sees its name; everybody else sees that it is one they can’t open. A blank line a new paragraph There are no images or HTML.

Type @ and the start of somebody’s handle, and the radio offers people to mention: everybody who has said something on the channel you are tuned to, everybody those messages mention, and everybody on Who’s online, alphabetically, never you. The first @ asks for Who’s online once. A mention is drawn as the person’s name, which opens their profile, and where you are mentioned your name is filled in, so you can see it. Nothing moves or lights up when one arrives. If they switched on When somebody @mentions me, they are told, as they were before. You can also call a role: @moderator calls every moderator, and anybody signed on can call it, which is how to ask our moderators for help. Moderators, directors, board members and administrators can call @director, @board and @administrator too. The roles you can call come first in the list, each saying what it calls. A role you call is drawn in the mention’s colour with nothing to press, because there is no profile behind it, and filled in where it is a role you hold. Everybody holding it who switched on When somebody @mentions me is told, where they can hear the room, and the notification says which role. Nobody is told who holds a role, or how many people were told. The word on its own is the role: @moderators stays words, and nobody can have a role’s word as a username. A call of @moderator from somebody who is not a moderator also leaves a note on the moderators’ desk, with who called, when, where and the words, so it waits for a moderator who was not listening; it goes when a moderator closes it, or after thirty days. Privacy has the rest.

Press Picture and choose a screenshot or a photo, or paste one into the message box. The radio redraws it in your browser before it goes, which takes off where it was taken and everything else the camera wrote into it. It shows you the picture first, above the box, as it will be sent, with the name of the file you picked, and nothing has gone anywhere yet. Then: Say what is in it, if you like is a description, up to 280 characters. It is offered, never required, and it is what a screen reader hears. Remove the picture takes it off the message. It goes with your next Transmit, with words or without. It is deleted when its message goes, and one you never send is deleted within the hour. Pictures on the channel have no public address. Only people signed on can see them, and the same norm as a screenshot applies to passing one on.

The last part of the radio is for the radio itself, rather than a room or a film. Just above it, under the heading You, are Profile, Account and Sign off, listed here too. Join this room’s call is under Where you are, and Add my spot, Host this film and Screen a video are under Watching together. Profile, Account, Notifications and Themes are edged in the readout’s amber while their trays are open, as Who’s online is. Every long tray ends in a button that closes it, Close Profile, Close Account, Close Themes, Close Notifications, Close stickers and Close your messages, so you need not scroll back up to the button that opened it; closing puts you back on that button. Control What it does Shown New messages to a screen reader: on New messages are announced to a screen reader as they arrive, at every size. Press to switch it off. always Speak new messages aloud: off Press to have the radio read each new message out in your own device’s voice, handle first, with a burst of static before and after; at the Gentle setting, the words without the static. It never reads your own messages or what was already there: Read aloud, under a message’s three dots, reads any one of them when you ask. when your device has a voice Clear the channel Clears the channel you are tuned to. See what moderators see. to moderators Themes Opens the radio’s themes, each with a little picture of itself, in groups. Everyday: Match my device, Amber, Daylight, High contrast, Solarized dark and Solarized light. Low stimulation: Warm Light, Cool Dark, Plant Green and Red Light, the dial’s low-stimulation modes on the radio alone, so the room keeps its own colours; each is the radio exactly as it is in that mode, with no drawing and nothing that moves. Radio faceplates: Green screen, Red readout and Teal glow. Worlds, with drawings: Biophilic, Star Stuff, LCARS, Max Glitter, Solarpunk, Biomechanical, Greeble, Crip Cyborg, Unicorn Poop, Wabi-sabi, Black Leather Lagoon, Kelp Forest, Fairy Lights and Cloud City, and Winamp skins: Zelda Amp, Microchip, ASCII-Amp, Super Mario Land Amp, Dig Dug Amp, deviantAMP, HP 49G, Winamp Mario, The Cube, Pip-Boy 3000, Game Boy and TI-82; and GeoCities pages: Divine Louise Brooks, Paula’s Page, Shop Til U Drop!, mansnhomepage, Double U for W, Beatnik Termites, The Green Room and Sarah’s Room; and Ryan’s favourite games: Castle Crashers, Dragon Age: Inquisition, Metroid, Mega Man, Fable III, Skyrim, Doom, Portal, The Witcher 3, Grand Theft Auto V, The Legend of Zelda and Shadow of Mordor. Each world, skin, page and game has a drawing under the radio’s bar, along its foot, along the dividers between its parts, and down both sides just outside it on a rail of its own, and its own shape and lettering for the radio’s name and headings. The sides need room either side of the radio, so it keeps a little further from the edge of the window for them, and on a window as narrow as a phone they are left off. Press one and the radio and the call window are in it at once, on every page, until you choose another, and the radio’s line says what it is after. Match my device, where everybody starts, is High contrast if your device asks for more contrast, Daylight if it is set to light, and Amber otherwise, and it changes when your device does. Every theme keeps every word at least 4.5 to 1 against what it sits on, and High contrast at 7 to 1; every sentence stays in the radio’s own easy-to-read type. The bar you see before you sign on matches your device too. Escape closes it. always Let my theme move: off Under the themes. A drawing moves by itself at MAX GLITTER, growing, twinkling, glowing or breathing, and stands still at the other settings; press this to let yours move at every setting. Nothing in any of them flashes, nothing moves when a message arrives, and Solarized and Wabi-sabi never move at all. in Themes Profile, under You Opens, under the heading You, your profile card and sets, your props, your avatars, your chimeras, your pets, your badges and jobs, and your battle jacket. always Notifications Opens notifications for this device. always Pop out Moves the radio into a window of its own, at the size it is now, which stays open while you go from room to room. In that window it is Back into the page. where your browser lets pages talk to each other Account, under You Opens, under the heading You, your username, where you claim it, change its password or delete it, and Forget me. always Sign off, under You Signs you off and takes the radio away, on every page, until you sign on again. It also switches off notifications on this device. always What the themes are after. Solarized is Ethan Schoonover’s palette, with a darker bar on dark and darker inks for words on light, so every word clears 4.5 to 1; its eight accents are the stripe. Biophilic takes queering.earth’s paper, moss and rust, and its ivy and mushrooms grow after the garden in Helen Edgar’s Faery Yurt; see our entry on biophilic design. Star Stuff is after starstuff.earth. LCARS is after the computer screens of Star Trek: The Next Generation , designed by Michael Okuda; Star Trek is a trade mark of CBS Studios, and nothing of theirs is copied. Solarpunk is art nouveau’s vines round sunflowers and a solar panel; see our entry on solarpunk. Biomechanical is after H. R. Giger’s biomechanics, and copies nothing of his. Greeble is after the greebles, small parts glued onto models, that made the spaceships of Star Wars look built; Star Wars is a trade mark of Lucasfilm. Crip Cyborg draws the kit some of us live with, a CPAP hose, an oxygen line and oxygen on a rack, a PEG tube and its port, and a prosthetic leg; see our entries on cyborgs and crip. Cloud City is after the city in the clouds of Bespin in The Empire Strikes Back , in the colours of randocloud.cloud; Star Wars is a trade mark of Lucasfilm, and nobody from the films is drawn. Max Glitter is the street’s own colours, Unicorn Poop is every pastel and gradients for no reason, and Wabi-sabi is a tea ring, a brush stroke and a crack mended in gold. Every drawing is drawn for the radio, and the worlds are Ryan’s list. The Winamp skins are after skins in the Winamp Skin Museum, Ryan’s picks, each credited to whoever its own readme says made it: Zelda Amp after LuigiHann’s Zelda Amp III, Microchip after Vad3K’s Microchip 2, ASCII-Amp after Pabo Wakataeo’s ASCII-Amp 2.0, Super Mario Land Amp after ronz’s skin of 2000, Dig Dug Amp after a skin of 2001 whose readme names its maker only by an email address, deviantAMP after sasso’s first skin, HP 49G after Arne Olav Storflor’s skin of his own calculator, Winamp Mario after winamp_mario, which names nobody, The Cube after Kuki’s the Cube v2, Pip-Boy 3000 after shadesmaclean’s (Neko-Sen’nin’s) skin for Spooky Door Productions, Game Boy after gameboy, which names nobody, and TI-82 after bLy’s (Erik Waldner’s) skin of 2000. No bitmap of any skin is used, and no character or mark from the games and machines they were after is drawn: hearts, bricks, pipes, pyramids, earth, keys, cubes and circuit boards are drawn for the radio. Kuki’s readme asks that nothing of the Cube be republished, and nothing is. The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario Land, Super Mario Bros. and Game Boy are trade marks of Nintendo; Dig Dug of Bandai Namco Entertainment; Fallout and Pip-Boy of Bethesda Softworks; deviantART of DeviantArt; HP of HP Inc.; TI-82 of Texas Instruments; Winamp of its owners. The GeoCities pages are after homepages kept in Restorativland’s GeoCities archive, Ryan’s picks, each credited as the page names its maker and otherwise by its own title and address: Divine Louise Brooks after a fan page made in Microsoft Publisher 97 at PicketFence/Gazebo/3270, which names nobody; Paula’s Page at RainForest/Jungle/2703; Shop Til U Drop!, Fran and Charlotte’s window-shopping page at RodeoDrive/Boutique/5707; mansnhomepage at Area51/Atlantis/7331; Double U for W after Dat’s double U for W!!! at Area51/Atlantis/7472; Beatnik Termites after the band’s unofficial home page at Area51/Orion/8820, designed by Benjamin T. Marotta; The Green Room, Aaron Ortiz’s page at Athens/Aegean/1213; and Sarah’s Room, Sarah’s home page at EnchantedForest/6203. Their colours were looked at and nothing on them is used: no picture, clip art, photograph or word, and nobody on them is drawn, not Louise Brooks, the band, or the child whose drawings fill mansnhomepage. No email address on any of them is repeated here, and nothing about anybody’s life. Ryan’s favourite games are after the games, each in its own palette and the shapes of its world, and no character, logo, emblem or symbol of any of them is drawn: castles and pennants, green rifts and gold filigree, blue cavern rock, an energy meter and ladders, a golden trail, snowy peaks and an aurora, riveted metal and fire, white panels and two portals, pines and a moon, a sunset and palms, the overworld’s trees and rocks, and rune medallions over black mountains and lava. Shadow of Mordor’s runes are after the game’s own, at Ryan’s ask: a gold ring with a mark glowing in it, each mark made up here out of a stave, branches, a crescent, prongs and dots, so none is a rune of the game’s and none a letter of Tolkien’s. Castle Crashers is The Behemoth’s; Dragon Age: Inquisition is BioWare’s, and Dragon Age a trade mark of Electronic Arts; Metroid and The Legend of Zelda are trade marks of Nintendo; Mega Man of Capcom; Fable III is Lionhead Studios’, and Fable a trade mark of Microsoft; The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim is Bethesda Game Studios’, and its names trade marks of Bethesda Softworks; Doom is a trade mark of id Software; Portal of Valve; The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is CD Projekt Red’s, and The Witcher a trade mark of CD PROJEKT; Grand Theft Auto V is Rockstar North’s, and Grand Theft Auto a trade mark of Take-Two Interactive; Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor is Monolith Productions’, for Warner Bros., and Middle-earth is J. R. R. Tolkien’s. With both New messages to a screen reader and Speak new messages aloud on, a screen reader user hears everything twice. At the foot of the radio are links to the house norms and to this guide.
The radio in a window of its own: Pop out

Every room is a page of its own, and the radio is on the page. Pop out, under Your radio, moves it into a browser window of its own, as big as it is and at the size it is in, and it stays there while you go from room to room in the window you came from. One radio at a time. While it is out, every page has a small bar where the radio was, saying In a window of its own, with Show it, which brings the window forward if your browser lets it, and Bring it back, which closes the window and puts the radio on that page. The bar sends nothing. It is about the page you came from. Where you are, This room, Be seen here and the room’s call are that page’s, and follow it as you walk. A link on the channel, the teleporter and a room in somebody’s profile open there, so the radio’s window keeps the radio. A page with no radio of its own, like the Healing Checkpoint, is no room to it. Films are in the page. A place in a film, @34:12, and Catch up move the film in the window you came from, and say so. Host this film, Add my spot and Follow need the radio on the page with the film, so bring it back for those. A call goes into a window of its own from there, the way Pop out on a call does, because the radio is the whole of its window. − and + still change the size, and make the window that size, as near as your browser allows. Back into the page closes the window, and so does closing it yourself. Your browser has to let stimpunks.world open a window. If it will not, the radio says so and stays where it was. On a phone the window is another tab.

Notifications opens a tray that switches this device on to be told about the CB, even with stimpunks.world closed. It is for this device only: a phone and a laptop are switched on, and choose, separately. Nothing is asked of your browser until you press Notify me on this device. Control What it does Everything, and anything added later Switches on every kind below, every message on World included, and any kind of notification the street adds later, so you do not have to come back and look. It leaves Show the words and the rooms you follow as they are. While it is on, every kind says on; switch one off and Everything goes off, and the rest stay on. When somebody @mentions me Tells you when a message on a channel you can hear, or a post in the forums that your claimed username can read, has @ and your handle in it, or calls a role you hold, and when an edit puts it in. Pressing a forum one opens the post. Off until you switch it on, like every switch here. When somebody replies to me Tells you when somebody replies to one of your messages on a channel you can hear, with who and where. Only your own messages: one sent under a claimed username tells only that username, and a reply in a room that keeps to itself tells nobody outside it. Never your own replies. When somebody messages me Tells you when somebody sends you a direct message, or asks to start a conversation, with who it is from. Pressing it opens the street with Messages open. Only a claimed username can be sent one. It never says how many are waiting. When somebody gives me props Tells you when somebody gives you props, which wait in Profile for you to confirm or reject, with who wrote them. Pressing it opens the street with Profile open at Your props. Only a claimed username has props to be told about. It never says how many are waiting. Every message on World Tells you about every message on the World channel. Something new in my Notifications in Tasks Only for Tasks’ readers, our directors, board members and administrators, so only offered when you are signed on with a moderator’s pass. Tells you whenever something arrives in your Notifications in Tasks: who did it and why it is yours, and the task’s name unless the words are off. Pressing it opens the task, or the comment. Never your own changes, and never what a description or a comment says. When an event I’m interested in starts Tells you up to five minutes before an event you said you are interested in starts, with where and when, and its title unless the words are off. Pressing it opens the chat page on that event. New events on World and in rooms I follow Tells you when somebody schedules an event on World or in a room you follow, with who, where and when it first starts, and its title unless the words are off. Never about an event you scheduled. Calls starting in rooms I follow, and the World call Tells you when somebody starts a call in a room you follow, or the World call. It never says who. Show the words of a message, a post, props, a task or an event’s title On, a notification shows the start of the message, the direct message, the post or the props, a task’s name or an event’s title; off, it says only who and where. On until you switch it off. Follow every room Follows every room you can go into at once, rooms that open later and the forums’ categories you can read included: every message on their channels tells you, and with Calls on, every call starting in one. World has its own switch, above. It can be a lot. Everything leaves it as you set it, and the rooms you follow one by one stay your list for when it goes off. A room that keeps to itself tells you only if you follow it there by name, so in one of those its own switch stays. Norah’s ask, 2026-10-21. The Feed and The Source keep their own switch too: what their feed bot says tells only a device that follows them by name. Follow and the room’s name In a room, follows it: every message on its channel tells you. The rooms you follow are listed under it, each with Stop following. While you follow every room, it shows only in a room that keeps to itself. Notify me on this device Your browser asks whether stimpunks.world may show notifications. Say yes, and this device is switched on with the choices above. Send me a test Sends one notification to this device, to see how they look. Switch off on this device Switches it off here and the street forgets this device. Signing off does the same. You are never told about your own messages, a room that keeps to itself tells only the devices that follow it, and a private room tells only people who can hear it. Nobody is told about props they gave. Pressing a notification opens its room. What your devices are told is kept for you for 30 days, without its words, under Past notifications on Your page. On an iPhone or iPad, notifications need iOS or iPadOS 26 or later: add stimpunks.world to your Home Screen (Share, then Add to Home Screen, with Open as Web App left on) and open it from there. Privacy says what is kept and what your browser’s push service sees.

Messages, the part under Channel, is for writing to one other person. Every username is claimed, so a message to one reaches whoever holds its password and nobody else. Your messages opens it, and while it is open it asks for your messages every few seconds, quietly; shut, folded or in a tab behind another, it asks nothing. Control What it does Let people message me Off until you switch it on. On, anybody with a claimed username can ask to message you. Off, nobody new can, and conversations already going go on. Write to a username and Open Opens your conversation with that username. So does Message under somebody’s card in their profile. Asking to message you Somebody’s first message, waiting for you, with its first words. Read their message to open it. Conversations Everybody you are talking with, whoever wrote last first, saying who wrote last and when, or that you are waiting for them to answer. A name opens the conversation. Accept and Reject On somebody’s first message. Accept, or simply answering, starts the conversation. Reject asks first, then deletes their message, and nobody is told; they can ask again. Send Sends what is in the box: Enter sends, and Shift and Enter starts a new line, as in the message box, so on a phone Return starts a new line and Send sends. Basic Markdown works, as on the channel, up to 2,000 characters. Your first message to somebody waits for them to answer it, and you can write nothing more until they do. Picture Only once a conversation is accepted: a first message is words only. Adds a picture to your message, the way Picture does on the channel: redrawn here first, with a description if you like, and gone when the message goes. You can paste one into the box too. Press it to open it larger, and Download keeps a copy. Sticker Only once a conversation is accepted. Opens the same tray as on the channel, your avatars, chimeras, pets and battle jacket, and sends a sticker of the one you press to this conversation. React The smiley on a message’s line, as on the channel, once a conversation is accepted. A reaction shows who pressed it, never how many, and pressing it again takes yours back. Reply The curved arrow on a message’s line, once a conversation is accepted. Answers that message, the way a reply does on the channel: Replying to above the box, Cancel reply or Escape to let it go, and a line above your message saying what it answers. More: Copy, Read aloud, Edit and Take back The three dots on a message’s line, as on the channel. Copy copies its words, and Read aloud reads that message out, as on the channel. On your own messages, Edit opens the words in a box where they were, and the message shows that it was edited; Take back asks first, then deletes it for both of you. More: Report On a message the other person sent you. Sends a copy of it, its picture if it has one, who sent it and when, your username and a note if you write one, to the moderators’ desk. They are not told. It is the only way a moderator ever sees a message. Block Under a conversation. Asks first, then stops them writing to you and you to them, and deletes your conversation for both of you. They are not told: if they write, they are told you are not taking messages from them. Unblock is under People you have blocked. All messages Back to the list. So is Escape. A conversation’s messages look and work like the channel’s: Markdown, links, a place in a film, an @name drawn as a name, a picture or a sticker, reactions, replies, and React, Reply and More on the message’s line, shown where the pointer or the keyboard is. A first message is words only, so a picture, a sticker, a reaction and a reply wait until it is accepted. Messages are not copied to the forums, because a conversation is the two of yours. Unless our administrators set direct messages otherwise, every message goes two weeks after it was sent, and a conversation keeps its latest hundred; one with nothing left in it is gone, and the next message asks again. Nothing counts messages, and nothing says whether somebody has read one or is typing. Nothing on the radio lights up when one arrives: switch on When somebody messages me to be told. They are sealed at rest, with a key of their own, and are not end-to-end encrypted: our server opens them to show them to the two of you. Privacy says what is kept.

Events are times somebody has scheduled, after Discord’s scheduled events (Ryan’s ask, 2026-10-23): a coworking hour in a room’s call, a film in a room, a meeting at a link off the street. Anybody signed on can schedule one, on World or in a room they can go into, and everybody who can go there can see it. They are under Events on the radio, after Unreads, and at the top of the channels on the chat page. Every time is in your own clock, whatever time zone whoever scheduled it is in. Control What it does On now in this room Under In this channel, while an event in the room you are in is going on: its title, which opens it, and when it ends. Events Opens the list: every event you can see, the soonest first, each with when, how it repeats and its next few times, how long it runs, where, who scheduled it, what it is about, and who is interested. It folds away again with Close Events at its foot. Where it is On the World call, on World’s channel, in a room’s call, in the room itself, or at a link off the street, which says it leaves the street and for where, like a link on the channel. A room’s name goes to the room, or to its channel on the chat page. Interested The usernames of everybody who has said they are interested, in alphabetical order, each opening their profile. Never how many, the way a reaction names who and never counts. I’m interested Puts your username on its list, or takes it off. With When an event I’m interested in starts switched on, this device is told as it starts. Whoever schedules one is interested from the start. Add to my calendar Gives your device a calendar file of the next time it happens. It is made in your browser and sent nowhere. Change it Only for whoever scheduled it, and for moderators. Opens the form with what it says now. Cancel just this time On a repeating event, for whoever scheduled it and moderators: cancels its next time for everybody, after asking once more, and the times after it go on. Cancel the event, or Cancel every time Cancels it for everybody, after asking once more. It cannot be put back. Schedule an event Opens the form: a Title; Where, which is World, the room you are in, or any room you can go into; How people join it, which is the call, the room or channel itself, or a link off the street; Date and Starts at, in your own time; How long it runs, up to a day; Repeats, which is every week, every other week, every month on the same weekday (the fourth Thursday, say, or the last Friday), or every weekday; and What it is, if you like, up to 2,000 characters with Markdown, as in a message. Schedule it puts it on the list for everybody who can see it. An event that happens once goes from the list when it ends. A repeating one keeps to the clock of whoever scheduled it, so it stays at the same time where they are when summer time starts or ends, and is there until they or a moderator cancel it. A room that keeps to itself has no events, because an event is listed outside it. Privacy says what is kept.

Teleport opens a box labelled Teleport to a room, or to @somebody and a list of every room on the street, in walking order. The room you are in says you are here; the others show their /tag, because the teleporter takes you to the room itself. Type to narrow it. It finds rooms whose names start with what you typed, then rooms with it inside a word of their name, so fire finds The Campfire, then rooms whose own description uses the word, with a few of those words shown. ↑ and ↓ move through the list, Enter goes to the room highlighted, and Escape puts the box away. Going is ordinary navigation. Nothing is sent to the channel, and nobody learns where you went. An @ looks for a person. Type @ and the list becomes the people on Who’s online, one line for each room they are in; type some of a handle to narrow it, and Enter goes to the room highlighted. Handles that start with what you typed come first. You are left out of it, and the letters you type are not sent anywhere. To search the words on every page rather than the rooms’ names, use the search box on the front page or the map.

When people watch the same film in a room, each person plays their own copy and pauses when they like. These help everybody find the same place. On the radio, Add my spot and Host this film are under the heading Watching together once a film or a live video on the page has started, and so is Screen a video, for moderators, on a page with a screen. Above them, under Hosting now, is everybody hosting a film on the street, this room’s first, with Catch up and Follow beside a host in your room and a link to the room beside any other. The heading is only there while one of them is, and the radio answers each of them under them. Small shows only the channel, so while the radio is Small its answers are under the readout instead. Control What it does An @time in a message Type @ and a time, like @34:12 or @1:02:03. Everybody sees it as a button that moves the film on their own page to that place. It never presses play. If the spot names a film or a room, it only moves that film in that room; anywhere else it says where the spot is. A time without the @ stays words. A live video has no place in it, so its spot is @live: pressing it gets that video’s play button ready on your page, or says it is already playing. @live is a button only when it names a video. Add my spot Writes the @time for you, with the film and the room, or @live for a live video. Host this film Everybody on the channel sees where you are in your film, whether it is playing, and in which room. In a room that keeps to itself, only radios tuned to that room’s channel see it. One person hosts a room at a time. On a live video, everybody sees that you are watching it live instead of a place in it, so you can tell the channel what is on. Putting your tab behind another pauses it; folding the radio or leaving the page stops it. Catch up Beside a host in your room: moves your film to where they are now. In an album or a playlist, it moves yours to the song they are on, and it still never presses play: it plays if yours was playing and waits if it was not. Beside a host on a live video, it gets the video’s play button ready instead, because everybody watching it live is at the same moment. Follow Beside a host in your room: keeps your film in step with theirs, at your own volume. In an album or a playlist it goes on to the next song with them, and anywhere they skip to. Pausing your own film, or pressing Follow again, stops following, so a break is always fine. There is no Follow beside a live video: there is no place in it to keep in step. Screen a video For moderators. Paste the address of one YouTube video, from youtube.com or youtu.be, and press Put it up: it plays on the page’s first screen, from the time in the address if it has one, in place of what the screen had. It is on your page only. Press Host this film once it plays, and everybody who presses Catch up or Follow beside you gets its play button on their own screen, with how long it runs, waiting for their press. The button under the screen puts back what was there. On a set you tune, like the Solarpunk Hermitage’s television, Looming Rocks’ stage or the Rebellion Rave Room’s big screen, it is tuned on the set instead, which stays off until they press play, and the set’s own controls tune back to its listing. A playlist’s address is refused. A spot’s room is a link. Following it takes you to the film’s play button, ready to start at that place when you press it. Nobody’s film moves unless they press something themselves. On a rack, Enter puts it up on the screen. Where the film is a card on a rack, which can play in its card or up on the room’s screen, a spot, Catch up and Follow all put the keyboard on the card’s button for the screen, so pressing it, or Enter, plays the film on the screen from the right place. And a film plays in one place at a time: putting a card’s film up on the screen stops it in its card, and playing it in its card takes it off the screen.

Every room has a voice and video call, run by 8x8. Join this room’s call on the radio opens it, and some rooms have a panel of their own that says Join the call as and your handle. A few rooms at Cavendish Coworking also let in people who are not signed on: they type The name you want to be called in the call and press Knock on the door. To find a call with people in it, open Who’s online: Calls going now names the World call and every room whose call has somebody in it. The World call is one call for the whole street. Join World call, under Who’s around, opens it from any page with the radio, in the same window as a room’s call, and press it again to leave. Anybody signed on can join; a guest cannot. You are in one call at a time, so joining the World call leaves the room’s call, and the other way round. Like every call it hangs up when you leave the page, and that includes going to another room, because every room is a page of its own, unless you pop it out into a window of its own. It is also the World room’s own call, so, as in any room, people seen in the World room are shown who is in it; nobody else is shown who is in it before they join. The call opens in a window of its own in the bottom left corner. Control What it does CALL and the room’s name Which call this is. Move, the six dots Drag the dots, or any part of the bar that is not a button, to put the call somewhere else. Or press the dots: they take the keyboard and say how it works, and then the arrow keys move the call 24 pixels a press and Home puts it back in its corner. Pop out Moves the call into a window of its own, which stays open while you go from room to room. Not at Small or Stamp, where there is no room for it on the bar. − and + Smaller and larger: one press goes from Large, the whole window, to Regular, where a call opens, to Small, a tile in the corner, to Stamp, the size of a postage stamp, or back up. Each says which size it goes to, and says so when the call is already as small or as large as it goes. Leave the call Hangs up. Leaving the page hangs up too, unless the call is in a window of its own, so while a call is up links on the radio open in a new tab and the browser asks before you leave the page any other way. In the call now: Who is in the call, if you have Be seen here on and the radio open. Inside the window is 8x8’s own screen. Your browser may ask about your camera and microphone so it can show a preview, but both start off, and nothing goes to the call until you join there. Folding the radio leaves the call running.
Following a link during a call

Every room is a page of its own, and a page that goes takes its call with it. So while a call is open on the page (Ryan’s ask, 2026-10-24): Anything on the radio that would leave the page opens in a new tab instead: a room’s #tag or a link on the channel or in a conversation, a room on Who’s online or Unreads, a favourite room on somebody’s profile, the teleporter and Take to the forums. The radio says so beside the link: That opened in a new tab, so your call stays up where it is. The guest bar’s teleporter does the same for a guest in a call. With no call up, links take you there as they always do. A link that stays on the page stays put, such as a channel on the chat page or a spot in a film in this room, and a link off the street opens in a new tab as it always has. A press with Ctrl, Cmd or Shift held is your browser’s to decide. Every other way off the page asks first. A link in the room itself, Back, or closing the tab brings up your browser’s own Leave site?, in its own words. Leaving the call, or popping it out, stops the asking. If your browser will not open a new tab, the radio says so, and you stay where you are, call and all. To walk about the street with the call instead, use Pop out.
A call that follows you: Pop out

Every room is a page of its own, and going to another room closes the page you were on, with its call. To keep a call while you walk about the street, press Pop out on the call’s window. The call moves into a browser window of its own and stays there while you go from room to room in the window you came from. You join again in the new window. A call cannot be carried from one window to another without starting over, so the new window opens on 8x8’s first screen, camera and microphone off, and you press Join there. The radio knows where it is. On every page, the call’s button stays pressed: Join World call for the World call, and Join this room’s call when you are back in the room it came from. Show the call window, under Who’s around, brings the window to the front. Pressing the call’s pressed button hangs up and closes the window. Still one call at a time.
