Popping out another call puts it in the same window in place of the first, and joining a call in a page hangs up the one in the window. Leave the call in the window hangs up and closes it, and so does closing the window. The window has no radio in it, so it does not show who is in a room’s call before you join; the radio in the room still does, to anybody seen there. Your browser has to let stimpunks.world open a window. If it will not, the call’s window says so and the call stays where it was. On a phone the window is another tab, and a phone may stop the camera or microphone of a tab that is not in front.

Profile, under the radio’s heading You, opens a tray there. Every section in it starts folded up, so the tray first shows only their headings, which are buttons: press one to open that section, and again to fold it. A section is only fetched from the street when you open it, and again each time you open it or Profile; any number can be open at once, and a new page starts with them all folded. The sections are your profile card, your profile sets, your props, your avatars, your chimeras, your pets, your badges and jobs, and your battle jacket. Every drawing in it, your avatars, your chimeras, your pets, your badges, your battle jacket and each patch on it, has a Download button that saves it as a picture on your own device. The picture is made in your browser and sent nowhere.

What anybody signed on to the CB sees when they press your name. Only a claimed username has one, and whatever you fill in is shown; a part left empty shows nothing, and nothing on it says when you joined. Edit my profile card opens it in a window of its own, with your card drawn beside the choices, again after every change (on a phone, its top stays in sight above them). See my card as others do opens it as anybody else sees it. Part What it is Theme One of the radio’s themes, for the colours of your whole profile. Left at None, everybody sees it in their own radio’s theme. Banner A theme’s drawing, along the top of your card, on its own theme’s colours. Decoration A ring drawn round the avatar you wear, in your card’s colours: flowers, ivy, stars, gears, flames, jack-o’-lanterns, two otters in a ring of kelp, cloud cars over a striped sun and more. You need to be wearing an avatar for it to show. Frame A band of your card’s theme round all four sides of your profile, outside it: briar, ivy, brass and rivets, fairy lights, a film strip, a graveyard gate, kelp fronds, the portholes of a city in the clouds and more. Effect Drawn over your profile in your card’s colours: butterflies, fireflies, falling petals, snow, shooting stars and more. Black Leather Lagoon is a whole scene in that room’s own colours, and pairs with the theme of the same name, the Graveyard gate frame and the Jack-o’-lanterns decoration, after the room and The Cramps: a drive-in screen in black water with a sea serpent of our own rising in front of it, poison ivy down the sides, leopard print along the foot, a finned hot rod and bats, with nobody real drawn, and its credit on your card. When your profile opens, and then once a minute while it is open, the serpent rears up out of black water across the whole profile, with mist and a flurry of bats, and sinks back after about nine seconds; like every effect’s pass, only at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move. Otters in the kelp is the other scene, in the Kelp Forest theme’s colours, and pairs with that theme, the Kelp fronds frame and the Otters in kelp decoration: sea otters floating on their backs in sunlit kelp, one with a strand of kelp across it and a shell on its chest, one rolling over, one swimming back and forth below, and bubbles rising across the profile. When your profile opens, and once a minute, the kelp forest grows up through the whole profile and a big otter swims up, rolls once, floats with its eyes shut and drifts away. It is after the Arcade’s Otterly Adorbs, and like it, floating fills nothing. Flying Fairy is the third scene, in the Fairy Lights theme’s colours, and pairs with that theme and the Fairy lights frame: the faeries of Helen Edgar’s Faery Yurt, no two dressed alike, flying across your profile from either side, darting and hovering and dropping petals, with a garland of fairy lights over your banner and a faery sitting on it. When your profile opens, and once a minute, a dusk comes up over the whole profile with sparkles along its top, and a big fairy in a crown of roses and a cloak of moss rises into it, opens her butterfly wings and beats them slowly while petals and leaves fall round her, and fades after about nine seconds. Cloud City is the fourth, in the Cloud City theme’s colours, and pairs with that theme, the Portholes frame and the Cloud cars decoration, after the city in the clouds of Bespin in The Empire Strikes Back: dusk over a sea of cloud, a striped sun going down behind it, the city standing out of the cloud on its stalk with its windows lit, and two cloud cars holding station, with nobody from the films drawn, and its credit on your card. When your profile opens, and once a minute, the sunset comes up over the whole profile with a sea of cloud along its foot, the city rises out of the cloud with its windows lighting from the top down, the sun sinks, and a pair of cloud cars flies out from the city towards you, and it all fades after about nine seconds. Howling Wolf, Starward Dreaming, Leaping Dolphins and Autumn Falls are scenes in colours of their own, over any card: a wolf on a crag raising its head and howling at a full moon, and when your profile opens the night comes up, the moon rises and two wolves on a far ridge answer; the stars and the Milky Way seen lying on your back in a clearing beside a fire, whose embers rise and become stars, and when your profile opens the trees close round it, a shower of embers goes up and a star falls, its flames swaying slowly and never flickering; dolphins leaping in arcs across a sea dappled by the setting sun, and when your profile opens a pod leaps across the whole of it; and a big tree in autumn colours dropping its leaves into piles, children popping up out of them and one in a wheelchair throwing leaves up, and when your profile opens the leaves come down all over it and pile up along its foot. Part of each stays along the edges and in the banner. The rest crosses your whole profile from time to time, words and all, and only for people whose radio is at MAX GLITTER or set to Let my theme move; for everybody else that part is not drawn at all. Face for your name One of the street’s typefaces, for your name on your card and nothing else. Every sentence stays in the radio’s own face. Nameplate A strip of a theme’s drawing under your name on Who’s online. Pronouns As you write them, beside your name. Tagline One line of your own, up to 100 characters, under your name on your card and beside it in the community directory. About you A few hundred characters. Markdown works as it does on the channel. Links Up to five, each starting with https://, shown as you typed it with its site after it. Your favourite room A room on the street, from the list, and a line on why. Who can open your card The community, anybody signed on to the CB, as every card was until 2026-10-26 and as yours is until you choose; Only me, which also takes your nameplate off Who’s online and you out of the community directory; or Anybody with the link to your profile’s own page, signed on or not. Show my profile in the community directory Off until you tick it. Ticked and saved, your username, nameplate, tagline, pronouns and the avatar you wear are listed in the community directory, and your name there opens your card. The editor shows your line as it will look while it is ticked. Save my card keeps it; Cancel, Escape or a press outside leaves it as it was, and if you have changed anything since you last saved, it asks first: Save and close, Close without saving or Keep editing. Clear my card asks once more, then empties it, takes your nameplate off Who’s online and takes you out of the community directory. A moderator can do the same to a card that breaks our covenant, and nothing else of yours changes: privacy says so. Every drawing on it moves only where the radio’s drawings do, at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move, and nothing in it flashes. An effect’s pass is the one drawing on the radio that crosses words, which is why it is there only then: switching Let my theme move off, or the dial down from MAX, takes it away.
Your profile’s own page, to share

Every profile has a page of its own, at stimpunks.world/profile.html# and the username (Helen Edgar’s question, 2026-10-26), and the link to it is under the card in every profile on the radio, and in your card’s editor under Who can open your card. The page shows the card and the tabs its owner shows on the CB, to whoever its owner chose: only themselves, anybody signed on, or anybody with the link. Props, chat statuses and messages are never on it; somebody signed on gets Props for and Message buttons there that open them on the radio. Copy the link on the page copies its address. Every part of the card is drawn there, frame, effect, banner, decoration, name face and nameplate, and its animations move at MAX GLITTER by themselves, or at any setting after Let it move on the card, which lasts for that visit. A line above the card says so, with a button that takes the keyboard to the dial; it is not shown at MAX GLITTER or in a low-stimulation mode. No search engine lists a profile. What it shows and keeps.

The community directory lists everybody on the CB who has ticked Show my profile in the community directory on their card (Ryan’s ask, 2026-10-23), for anybody signed on. Each line is the avatar they wear, their name, BASE for a moderator, their pronouns, their tagline and their nameplate, and pressing a name opens their profile, as it does on Who’s online. It is in alphabetical order. Find somebody narrows it by name, pronouns or tagline, in your browser, and sends nothing. At the top it says whether you are in it, and Edit my profile card there opens your card’s editor, where the box is. It never says how many people are in it, nor when anybody joined. What it keeps.

A set keeps your card’s look under a name you give it, so you can wear it again with one press: by mood, for the room you are in, or for what is on, Otters, Halloween or Fairy Lights. A set is your card’s theme, banner, decoration, frame, effect, name face and nameplate, and the avatar you wear. Your pronouns, your words, your links and your favourite room are not in a set, so they stay as they are whichever you wear. Only a claimed username has sets, and nobody else sees them: anybody who opens your profile sees only what is on your card. Save as a set, under the sets in Profile, takes your card as you last saved it with Edit my profile card, and the avatar you wear, and names it. To make another, change your card, save it, and save it as a set again. Pressing a set wears it: your card takes its look at once, and the avatar it wears is put on, or taken off if it wears none. The set your card is wearing says On your card now. If a set’s avatar has been deleted, it says so, and wearing it leaves the one you wear. Each set has a strip of its banner on it, and says in words what it holds. Change under each set has Update it to my card as it is, which puts your card and the avatar you wear into it in place of what it held, Rename it and Delete it. Update and Delete ask once more. Clear my card leaves your sets. Forget me and Delete my account delete them.

A prop is a sentence or a short paragraph thanking somebody, acknowledging them or celebrating them, usually for something they did for you or for the community. Yours are on the Props tab of your profile, and only a claimed username has one. Show my props on the CB opens your Props tab. It starts off. While it is off, nobody can give you props and your tab shows none; what you confirmed is kept for when you switch it on again. Nothing goes up until you say so. Props people give you wait under Waiting for you, each with who wrote it. Confirm puts it on your Props tab. Reject asks first, with Yes, reject it or Leave it waiting, then deletes it; nobody is told. The ones you confirmed are under On your profile, newest first. Take it off my profile asks first, with Yes, take it off or Leave it up. See my Props tab as others do opens your profile on that tab. Giving somebody props is on their Props tab: open their profile, write in the box headed Give and their name, and press Send it to and their name. It needs a claimed username, and their tab open. Markdown works as it does on the channel, up to 500 characters. It waits for them to confirm it, shown to you under Waiting for them to confirm, with Take it back, and one of yours waits for each person at a time. If they reject it, it stops waiting. Take it back is on what you wrote once it is up, too. Being told when props arrive. Nothing on the radio lights up when somebody gives you props, so they wait here until you next open Profile, unless you switch on When somebody gives me props under Notifications. Then the device is told who wrote them, and pressing the notification opens Profile here. Whoever wrote them is never told whether you were. Nothing counts props: nobody is shown how many anybody has, or has waiting. Nothing about when one was written is kept. For thanks the whole community reads, there is Props & Gratitude in the forums.

Pressing a handle on the channel, or a name on Who’s online, opens that person’s profile over the page. On the left is their card, in the theme they chose, with whatever they filled in; press the avatar they wear to open it larger. On the right are tabs: Avatars, the one they wear large and first and the rest if they have chosen to show them; Pets; Badges and jobs, where a badge comes only from what they show, their jobs and Pet Parent if their pets are shown; and Battle jacket, if they have chosen to show it, with every patch sewn on listed under it, each with the room it came from, linked to where it lies; Chimeras, if they have chosen to show them, each with its name and which animal gave which part; and Props, if they have opened it, each with who wrote it, whose name opens their profile, and a box to give them props. Under their card, Message and their name opens your conversation with them, if you have a claimed username. The arrow keys move between the tabs. Close, Escape or a press outside puts it away, and the keyboard goes back to the name you pressed.

Every avatar you have kept, from the Bodymind Booth or the Dress-Up Den, with its drawing, its name and what you wrote about it, which is all a screen reader hears for it. Wear it on the CB shows that one beside your name on Who’s online, and large in your profile, and Take it off the CB shows none. One at a time; change whenever you like. It needs a claimed username. Show my avatars on the CB shows the rest in your profile too, the one you wear first, with their names and what you wrote. It needs a claimed username, and it starts off. Name it and say what it shows gives it a name and your own words for it, then Save or Leave it as it is. Dress it at the Den and Change it in the booth take it back to be changed. Download saves its picture. Delete it asks first, with Yes, delete it or Keep it.

Every chimera you have kept from Chimera Obscura, with its drawing, its name, and which animal gave which part, which is what a screen reader hears for it. Rename it gives it a new name, then Save or Leave it as it is. Put it back on the table opens it in Chimera Obscura to change it. Download saves its picture. Delete it asks first, with Yes, delete it or Keep it. Show my chimeras on the CB shows them in your profile, with their names. It needs a claimed username, and it starts off. Nothing about when you made one is kept.

Every pet you have adopted, with its drawing, its name and when you adopted it. Rename or Name them gives one a name; the name it came in under is kept on the list of everybody adopted. Download saves their picture. Show my pets on the CB lets anybody on the CB press your handle, on the channel or on Who’s online, and see them. It needs a claimed username, and it starts off.

Your badges, each drawn and named with what it is for. Most are made by jobs; Pet Parent by having adopted a pet, and Rescue Ranger by having rescued an animal in this browser, which only you are ever shown, because nothing on the street knows who rescued. A badge is worked out every time and is kept nowhere; nothing counts them. Download saves a badge’s picture, on the radio’s own dark ground. The jobs you have handed in at the Adventurer’s Guild, once Keep my jobs in my Profile is switched on there, beside the box where codes are handed in. It starts off, and switching it off deletes them here. Each job links to its place on the board. Show my jobs on the CB lets anybody on the CB who opens your profile see your jobs and their badges. It needs a claimed username, and it starts off. Nothing about when you did a job is kept, so nobody is shown that.

A denim jacket from the back, with every patch you have picked up sewn on, each its own size and shape, in the order the street lists them. Under it, their names in words, and Download, which saves the jacket’s picture. Your patches, one at a time lists every patch on it, each with its own Download. Patches lie about the street, and some are on a counter in a shop, free to take. In a room, signed on, a patch’s Pick it up or Take one puts it on your jacket. Where the patches are lists every one, with its room, and says which are on your jacket. Show my battle jacket on the CB lets anybody on the CB who opens your profile see it. It needs a claimed username, and it starts off.

Account, beside Profile under the radio’s heading You, opens a tray there with your username and Forget me: what you are signed on as and what the street keeps under you, where Profile is what you show. It ends in Close Account.

Claimed when you joined. Every username on the CB is claimed, on the joining page: only your own password signs on as it. The recovery code is shown once, when you join. It is the way back in if you forget your password, at the front desk. A reset code by email, or one from a moderator, works there too. Email for password recovery says which address a reset code goes to, if you gave one. Add one or Change it asks for Your email address and Your password, to be sure it is you, then Keep this address; Take it off asks for your password, then Take it off. It is shown to nobody but you. Offered only while recovery by email is switched on. Change my password asks for Your password now, A new password and The same again, then Change it. Every other device signed on as you is signed off. Delete my account asks for your password, then Yes, delete my account or Keep it. It cannot be undone. Five wrong passwords lock a claimed username for fifteen minutes.

A second step after your password, so somebody who learns it still cannot sign on as you. Anybody can turn it on, and from 2 November 2026 moderators and staff must: a staff username without it is on the CB as an ordinary member until it is set up, and You on the radio says so. Privacy says what is kept. Set up an authenticator app shows a QR code to scan with any authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Aegis, 2FAS, or a password manager), the same key written out to type in, and a link that opens an app on the same device. Then type the six-digit code it shows and press Turn it on. Add a passkey asks your device to make one: your fingerprint, your face or its screen lock. Give it a name, like My phone, so you can tell your passkeys apart. You can add several, on different devices. Backup codes are shown once, when the first step goes on: ten codes, each good once, for when you cannot use your app or passkey. Copy them and keep them somewhere safe. Make new backup codes asks for your password and replaces them. Signing on asks for your password and then one step: Use a passkey, the code from your app, or Use a backup code instead. Take it off, beside a step, and Turn two-step sign-in off ask for your password. Adding or taking off a step signs every other device off. Lost every step? A backup code gets you in. Otherwise a moderator can reset your username, which takes the second step off; your recovery code, or a reset code we email you, changes your password and still asks for the second step.

Forget me deletes everything the street keeps under your handle: your avatars, your chimeras, your pets, your jobs, your patches, your profile card and its sets, your props, your chat status and whether any of them are shown. It asks first, with Yes, forget me or Keep them. The animals stay on the list of everybody adopted, with nothing connecting them to you.

The chat page is every room’s channel on one page, laid out the way chat is (Ryan’s ask, 2026-10-22). It is the radio itself, docked into the page at its largest rather than over it, so everything the radio does it does there, in your radio’s theme. Unreads and the channels are down the left, the one you pick is in the middle, with its room’s name and what the room is about over its messages and the box to write in, and what is about that channel, who is around and the rest of the radio are on the right. Part What it does Unreads At the top of the left, above the channels (Ryan, 2026-10-24, because under them it was a long scroll away): World, the rooms you follow and your conversations, while something new has been said in them. Press one and its channel or conversation is put in the middle. Channels Every channel you can hear, in groups, each folding under its name. Community is World, the Community Center, Community Care, Coping, Pets, Show Your Work and every room at Cavendish Coworking. Staff is the Town Hall’s private rooms, Tasks, the Office and the forums’ staff categories, each shown only to the people who can go in, so it is not there at all for anybody else. Then every room is grouped by its tags (Ryan’s asks, 2026-10-24): what the room is for, like Music, Pets, Calm, Coping, Homes or Make/build, each group A to Z unless you choose another order (below), passing over a leading The, A or An, so The Den is with the Ds. Community’s rooms are under their tags as well, so Dead Tired Society is in Community and in Coping, and a room with more than one tag is in each of those groups, so you may meet a room more than once. Staff’s rooms and World are never under a tag. The forums’ other categories come after The forums, under Forums. A channel with something new in it since you last read it is in bold with a dot, as on Unreads, and never with a number. Events At the top of the channels: every event you can see, put where the channel was, in the middle, with Schedule an event. It says on now while one is. Its address is chat.html#events, and one event’s is chat.html#events/ and the event’s id, which is where a notification about it opens. What is on now in the channel you picked is also under In this channel. Direct messages Your conversations, in the list after Community: All messages, which is the list with Let people message me and a box to write to a username, then everybody you are talking to, the latest first, with asking beside anybody waiting for your answer and a dot beside anybody who has written since you last read it. Picking one puts the conversation where the channel was, in the middle, as tall as the page, and picking a channel puts the channel back. A conversation is not in the page’s address, so Back goes to the channel before. On the chat page Messages is here and not on the right. Sort the channels under tags Under Find a channel: A to Z, where everybody starts; Recently active, the channel with the newest message first; Most active, the channel with the most messages in the last two weeks first; or My own order (below). By activity, channels with nothing said in them come after, A to Z, and the street’s bot, which says each arrival on The Feed’s and The Source’s channels, counts for neither. Community and Staff keep their own order. The channels are put in order only when the page opens, when you choose an order, and when you press Sort again, never as messages come in, so nothing moves while you are reaching for it; a line under it says when they were sorted. Nobody is shown a time or a number for any channel. Your browser remembers the order you chose (the privacy page). My own order and Arrange The channels under each tag, and More rooms, in the order you put them in, each group on its own, so moving The Den in Music leaves it where it was in Pets. Arrange puts ↑ and ↓ beside every channel, Move up and Move down, named for the channel and its group; on a channel, Alt and ↑ or ↓ moves it too, and you can drag one onto another, landing before it on its top half and after it on its bottom half. Tab goes from a channel to its own two buttons. A line says where each channel has gone, after and before which. Done arranging puts the buttons away. A channel you have not placed, like a room that opens later, comes after the ones you have, A to Z. It is kept on our server under your username, so it is the same on every device you sign on with, and it is shown to nobody else; Forget me and deleting your username delete it (the privacy page). Find a channel Narrows the list as you type, by a room’s name or by what it is about, the way the teleporter finds rooms, and by a group’s name: pets finds every room under Pets. ↓ goes from the box into the list. It finds a conversation by the username too. Picking a channel Press its name. The channel is in the page’s address, after a #, so Back goes to the one you were on before and a link like chat.html#the-den opens on The Den. A #tag in a message, and a room on Unreads or Who’s online, opens that room’s channel here; a /the-den in a message opens the room’s own page. In the list one channel is a stop for Tab, the one you are on, and ↑, ↓, Home and End move between them. On a narrow screen the list folds under one button that names the channel you are on, and picking one folds it again and puts you on its name. Go to the room Under the channel’s name: the room itself, where its channel is the radio’s This room. World’s goes to the World room. In this channel The radio’s In this channel, for the channel you picked: Be seen here shows you in that channel’s room, and Join this room’s call is that room’s call. It changes nothing about the radio on every other page: its size, whether it is folded, where it sits, and World or This room stay as you left them there. It listens only while the page is in front of you, to the one channel you picked.

Your page is the radio’s You part on a page of its own (Ryan’s ask, 2026-10-25: “Desktop notifications come and go”). It is the radio itself, docked into the page at its largest, as the chat page is, in your radio’s theme. Your page, under You on the radio anywhere else, goes there. Part What it does You The wide column: Profile, open when the page opens with its sections folded, Account and Sign off. Past notifications Everything the CB’s notifications told your devices in the last 30 days, newest first, each said the way the notification said it, with when it was sent, and a link to where it was about. It keeps only what a device was actually sent, so what you switch on decides what is in it, and something told to your phone and your laptop is here once. It never keeps the words: they are read again from wherever they still are each time you look, so a message gone at its two weeks, or taken off, is here only as that there was one, and a direct message or props never shows its words here. One you had not seen yet has a dot, and keeps it while the page is open; it is never counted. The list is asked for again at most once a minute while the page is in front of you. Clear my past notifications asks you once more, then deletes all of it. Unreads, Messages and Your radio As on the radio anywhere: what is new to you, your conversations, and the radio’s own switches, Notifications among them. Speak new messages aloud and a moderator’s Clear the channel are not here, because the channel is not shown; Speak aloud stays as you set it on every other page. Where you are, the channel and what is about it, who is around, Events and Watching together are not on Your page, because it is about you and not about a room; they are on the radio everywhere else, and on the chat page. It changes nothing about the radio on every other page. Nobody else can open your past notifications, a moderator included (the privacy page).

The forums are the CB’s for whatever needs longer than the channel’s two weeks: topics in categories, after Discourse. Only a claimed username can read or write in them, so claim yours from Account first. They wear your radio’s theme, its colours, its face for headings and its drawing, or another one you choose for the forums alone at the foot of them. For what needs longer than a day: the forums, under the radio’s Channel part, goes there. Every category is a room on the CB (Ryan’s call, 2026-10-21). Open a category, or a topic in it, and the radio’s This room is that category’s room, The forums: Coping, say, with its own channel, Be seen here, call and Follow this room; go to another category and it retunes, without the page loading again. A category inside another is the room of the one it is in, so the whole of Team Docs is one room. The forums’ home, Latest, Mentions and a search are the forums’ own room, The forums. A category’s room is for exactly the people who can read the category, so a staff category’s channel, its call and who is seen in it are its staff’s alone, and you are never shown a category you cannot read anywhere on the radio: not in a #tag, the teleporter, Who’s around or Unreads. Take to the forums from a category’s channel starts the topic in that category. Part What it does Categories Every category you can read, in groups, each saying what it is for and how long a topic stays after its last post: a week, three months, six months or for good. A few are for our moderators, directors or board, and nobody else is shown that they are there. A category can hold others, listed under it at the side and on its own page, and its page lists every topic in it and under it; one that only holds others, like Team Docs and its Meeting Minutes, takes no topics of its own. Latest Every topic you can read, the one posted in most lately first. NEW marks a topic started since you first came, and NEW POSTS one with posts since you last opened it. Your browser works those out; nothing about what you read is sent to us. Forget what I have read, at the foot, clears it. New topic A category, a title and your post. Markdown works, and Preview shows how it will look. A link on a line of its own becomes a preview: a page’s title and description, a room on the street’s name, or a video’s title with a Play button that says how long it runs when that could be found out. Only moderators start topics in Announcements. A post is up to 20,000 characters, and a page in the Wiki or Team Docs up to 150,000, so a long document or a meeting’s minutes with their transcript go up whole. Markdown makes a table too: a row to a line, a | between cells, and a line of dashes under the first row, as | What | Who | then |---|---|. Add a poll Under a new topic, before you post it (Norah’s ask, Ryan’s calls, 2026-10-22), or under Change this topic, at the foot of a topic that has none, if you started it, edit a wiki it is in (Grantmaking’s directors and board, say) or are a moderator. Adding one to a topic posts nothing and moves nothing, so reply if you want people to know. Choose its kind, which never changes after: a show of hands, where everybody who can read the topic sees who picked what as the votes come in, and you can change your vote or take it back while it is open; or a sealed ballot, where nothing kept says who picked what, so nobody can see it, moderators included, a vote cannot be changed or taken back, and asks a second time before it goes, and nobody sees a number until it closes. Then the question (the title, if you leave it empty), two to twenty choices, one to a line, whether people can pick more than one, and the day it closes, or none, and you close it yourself. The poll stands under the post that opens the topic, says how many picked each choice in its own order, and is marked POLL in the lists. Whoever added the poll, whoever started the topic, or a moderator, can close it; a show of hands can be opened again, and a sealed ballot cannot, because votes after its results would tell who picked what. With only a few votes, a sealed ballot’s numbers can still say who picked what. A vote tells nobody. Start from a template Over the title of a new topic, wherever you can read Team Docs’ Templates. Pick one and press Use it: its title and words go into your topic, to change and fill in. Over words you have already written, it asks first. A pinned topic in Templates is its read-me, not a template. Tags Under the words of a new topic, up to five words to find it by, with commas between them, like grant-round: lower case letters, numbers and hyphens, and a space becomes a hyphen. A template brings its tags with it. On a topic, its tags are under the title, each a link to the topics in its category that carry it, and whoever started it, or a moderator, can change them under Change this topic, at the foot of it, with Tags and Save the tags, which moves nothing and marks no post edited. A category’s page lists the tags its topics carry, never how many, to show only one tag’s topics; Every topic shows them all again. A search finds a topic by its tags too. Add pictures or files Under any post you are writing. A picture is redrawn in your browser before it goes, which takes off what the camera wrote into it, and you can say what is in it. A file can be a PDF, plain text, Markdown, CSV, RTF, a Word, Excel, PowerPoint or OpenDocument document, or an EPUB, up to 5 MB, and goes exactly as it is. Up to six on a post, and thirty on a page in the Wiki or Team Docs. Take it off removes one before you post. In a post, pressing a picture shows it larger, and Save saves a file to your device. A picture in the words A picture stands below a post’s words unless you put it in them, for a screenshot in the middle of a how-to. Put it in the words, at the cursor does that, and so does pasting a screenshot into the box you are writing in or dropping a picture on it. It goes in as a line of its own, ![what it shows](pic:…): move the line to move the picture, and what you say is in it goes between the brackets. Show it below the words instead takes it back out of them. @ and a name Mentions somebody. Typing @ and a letter lists the people in the topic, anybody claimed on Who’s online, and anybody who started or last posted in a topic you can read (and, if you can open Tasks, everybody it can assign): ↑ and ↓ move, Enter or Tab puts the name in, Escape leaves what you typed. A mention shows as their name, which opens their profile, and tells them if they switched on When somebody @mentions me. The roles you can call (@moderator, and for our moderators @director, @board and @administrator) come first in the list and tell everybody who holds them and can read the category. MENTIONS YOU marks a post that mentions you, or a role you hold. Mentions The topics where somebody has mentioned you, or called a role you hold, the latest first, with the words around it. Worked out each time you look, and kept nowhere. The Wiki How to do things on the street, the CB and the forums, one thing to a page, kept for good. The post that opens each topic there is a WIKI PAGE: our moderators keep it up to date whoever started it, and it says who started it and who edited it last. Replies on a wiki page stay their writers’ own, and a wiki page goes only with its whole topic. Only moderators start pages there; anybody can reply to one. Team Docs For our moderators, directors, board and administrators only: the team’s own documents, kept for good. Field Guide is how we do things, Notes is notes worth keeping, Meeting Minutes holds a category for every year from 2024, a new one each January, and Templates is what new topics start from. Every page there is a WIKI PAGE, any of them can edit. Grantmaking For our directors and board. Every grant round is a topic tagged grant-round, kept for good: start one from the Grant Round template, and any director or board member can edit the post that opens it, to add their name to its Approvals, as in Notion’s Grants table; it says who edited it last. The rounds from that table were brought in at the time each was made there, under the username that made it, and each says brought from Notion, linked to its page there (Ryan’s ask, 2026-10-22). Grantmaking is not sealed the way the office is. A topic Every post in order, each with who wrote it and when. Reply answers that post, Quote puts its words in your reply, React adds a reaction, named and never counted, and Edit and Take down are on your own posts. Pressing a name opens their profile on the radio. Each topic says the date it goes, unless somebody posts in it before then. Copied from the CB Messages taken to the forums, on the radio’s own readout, as they were sent. Take my message out is on yours, so you can take your words back out of somebody’s topic. Search Titles, posts, copied messages, file names and what pictures are said to show, in every topic you can read. Every word has to be there. Tasks and Office At the end of the bar, for our directors, board members and administrators, who can open Tasks and the office; nobody else is shown them. Tasks’ bar and the office’s have Forums, and each other. Colours for the forums The same as your radio, or any of its themes, for the forums alone. Kept in your browser. ← Back to … Above every view you reached from another one in the forums, saying which it goes back to. It goes back one step, not to the street, to where you were in that view, with the keyboard on the link you followed; pages of older topics you had opened are opened again. Your browser’s Back and Forward, and Alt or Cmd and ←, do the same. Starting a topic, or taking one down, takes the place of the step it was done on rather than adding one after it, so Back never lands on a finished form or a topic that has gone. A topic’s own controls are under Change this topic, at the foot of it after the reply box, so nothing stands between its title and its words. There a moderator can Pin a topic, which keeps it while it is pinned, Close it so only moderators reply, Move it to another category, chosen under Move it to another category, or Take the topic down. A moderator can also take down any post, from the post, and edit any page in the Wiki and Team Docs. Nobody gets a badge, nothing is counted but a poll’s votes, and the only notification is a mention, for somebody who asked for it. Privacy has what the forums keep.

Tasks are the team’s to-do list, moved here from EspoCRM, in the CB’s colours like the forums. Only directors, board members and administrators can read them, on a claimed username; everybody else is told nothing. Numbers are fine here: the list and the board say how many tasks match, a column how many it holds, and each choice of filter and each saved filter how many it would show. Part What it does List Every task that passes the filters, with how many of them there are. Until you pick whose, it shows yours: the tasks assigned to you and the ones you are also on, as the list, the board, the timeline and the feed all do. Until you pick statuses, it shows the ones still to do, and hides Completed and Canceled. It says who each task is assigned to and who else is on it, and Whose names everybody on it together, in alphabetical order. Group by puts the list under headings, after Notion’s By assignee: Whose puts each task under every person on it, assigned or also on it, so each person’s heading has all of theirs, with Nobody last; Tags puts it under each of its tags; Assigned to, Status and Priority once each. A heading folds its group away, and the column headings sort every group alike. A heading sorts by that column, and again the other way round; a task with nothing in that column goes last. A status is a coloured pill, after Notion’s: Not Started gray, Started light blue (Notion’s In progress), Completed green, Canceled brown and Deferred yellow, always with its name. OVERDUE marks a task past its due day that is not done. Rest the pointer on a task’s name, or land on it with the keyboard, and its preview shows beside it, after a moment: what happened to it last, the first parts of its description and its latest comments. Esc puts it away, and you can move the pointer onto it to read it. Nothing on it can be pressed; its own page has the whole of it. Board The same tasks in columns, after EspoCRM’s Kanban: by status, or by priority or who it is assigned to under Columns by, each column saying how many cards it holds. By status it shows every status but Canceled until you tick it under Status; by priority or person it shows what is still to do, as the list does. Drag a card to another column to change that one thing about it, or use its own Move to, which is how a keyboard, a screen reader or a phone moves it. A card names the task, links to it, and says what the columns do not: its status, priority, who has it and who else is on it, when it is due, and its tags. Timeline The same tasks across their days, after EspoCRM’s calendar timeline: a row for each person, with the days running across and each task a bar from the day it starts to the day it is due. A task stands in the row of whoever it is assigned to and in the row of everybody also on it, marked ALSO ON IT there; Everybody’s shows every person’s row, and yours or one person’s shows that row alone. A task with only one of those is on that day; a task with neither has no place on it, and the line above says how many. Days shown is a week, 2 weeks or 4 weeks, from a Monday; Earlier, This week and Later move along. Today is outlined, a bar that began before the days shown or runs on past them has a dashed, open end and says so, and two tasks on the same days stand one above the other. Every bar says its own days in words, and the timeline scrolls sideways in its own box on a narrow screen. A bar is filled with its tags’ colour, the first of them, and a bar with tags of more than one colour has stripes along its foot, one for each; the legend above says which tags wear which colour. Feed The same tasks as cards, after Notion’s Feed view, the one something last happened to first: a task’s name, what happened to it last and who did it, its status, priority, who has it and who else is on it, its days and tags, and its description, the first few parts of it with More for the rest. A checklist ticks there as it does on the task’s page, and Mark it completed and Open are on every card. A card says how many comments its task has and shows the latest two, and Comment writes one where the card stands; a comment puts its task first, as a change does. Until you pick statuses it shows every status but Canceled, so what was finished is there too. Twenty cards at a time, with Show more at the foot; a card you change stays where it is until the feed is drawn again. Tag colours Every tag has a dot of its colour beside its name, wherever a tag is shown. Tags take a colour by what they are about, because twenty-three colours could not be told apart: running things (Operations, Systems, Business Papers) are blue, money (Finance, Fundraising, Grantmaking, Outside Grants) orange, people (Community, Connection Requests, Networking/Social, Volunteering) aqua, gatherings (Meetings, Events) yellow, words (Editorial, Learning Center, Resource Research) magenta, the shop (Shop, Merch) green, and looking after ourselves (Professional Development, Coping, Time Off) violet. Weekly and Monthly say how often rather than what about, and wear none. The colours are one set for a light radio theme and one for a dark, each chosen so the words on a bar can be read, and a colour always comes with its tag’s name. Filters On the list, the board, the timeline and the feed alike: words in the name, Whose (yours, everybody’s, one person’s, or assigned to nobody; a task is somebody’s when it is assigned to them or they are also on it, so a task with three people on it counts for all three), when it is due (overdue, today, the next 7 days, this month, or never), and its status, priority and tags. Each choice says how many tasks it would show. Clear the filters starts again. Saved filters Above the filters. Save this view names the list, the board, the timeline or the feed as it is, filters, order, columns and days shown, and it is kept under your username, so it is there on any device you sign on with; or put it in place of one you already have. Each says how many tasks it shows now; a saved timeline, how many fall on its days. A timeline saved on this week stays on whichever week is this week. Picking one opens it; Delete beside it, once you are on it, deletes it and asks first. They are yours alone: nobody else sees them. Recurring Tasks that come round again, after EspoCRM’s: weekly, every 2 weeks or monthly. Each says how often, the next day it makes a task, how many days after that day the task starts and is due, and who it goes to. On that day the task is made by itself, within the hour after midnight in Colorado, the street’s clock, and the next day moves on; a monthly one keeps its day of the month, or the month’s last day when the month is shorter. A name can carry {week}, {year} or {month}, filled in from the day it is made: {week} is the ISO week, Monday to Sunday, and in a name with a week in it {year} is that week’s year, so the first days of January can still be the last week of the year before. Switch off makes nothing until it is switched on again, and then it starts from its next day still to come, without making the ones it missed. Each lists its next three and the tasks it has made, and a task it made says so. Deleting one leaves the tasks it made. Templates A task to start from: its name, description, tags, priority, who it goes to and how many days after it is made it starts and is due. Choose one under Start from a template on New task, or press Make a task from it on its page. A name or description can hold {name}, somebody’s name, and {contact}, {case} and {grant}, links to their records in the office; replace them in the form, with their name and with a link typed with [[, and Tasks will not make the task with one left in. When somebody fills in stimpunks.org’s Join form, the office makes their onboarding task from its template by itself, with their name and links to their join request and contact filled in; who it goes to is whoever the template says, so set that on the template. Each template lists the tasks made from it, and deleting one leaves them. Copy a link to this view The filters, the order and the columns live in the page’s address, so a bookmark keeps them and another director who opens the link sees the same list or board. Nothing is kept in your browser. A task Its status, priority, who it is assigned to and who else is on it, the days it starts and is due, when it was finished, its tags, who made it and who changed it last, and its description. Edit, Mark it completed and Delete, which asks first. A checklist in the description ticks in place, as in EspoCRM: a list item written - [ ] or - [x] is a box, and ticking it changes that box and nothing else, so two people ticking different boxes at once both keep theirs. A tick says who changed the task last, like any change. If the description has changed since the task was drawn, the tick is refused and the page says to look again. A recurring task’s boxes are shown and not ticked there; each task it makes starts with them as they are written. Notifications After EspoCRM’s notifications and Notion’s inbox: changes to the tasks you are assigned to, are also on or made, being put on or taken off a task, a task a recurring task made for you, an @mention of you in a description or a comment, comments on the tasks you are on, made or commented on, and comments in the office on what you added or commented on or that @mention you, newest first, for 30 days. Your own changes are never there. How many are unread is beside its name in the bar. At the top, Due lists your tasks that are overdue or due today or tomorrow. Open the task marks one read; Mark read and Mark all read do it without opening; Unread shows only those. Nobody else sees your notifications. To be told on a phone or a computer as well, switch on Something new in my Notifications in Tasks under Notifications on the radio. Comments Under every task, after EspoCRM’s stream posts and Notion’s comments: the conversation about it, oldest first, each with who wrote it and when, and a box at the foot to add one. A comment takes Markdown, and Preview shows how it will look; Ctrl or Cmd and Enter posts it. A comment tells whoever the task is assigned to, anybody else on it, whoever made it and anybody who commented on it before, in their Notifications, and anybody it @mentions; never the person who wrote it, and never its words, only that there is one and on which task. Open the comment there opens the task on it. Only whoever wrote a comment can edit it, in place, and it then says when it was edited; an edit tells only anybody it newly @mentions. Type @ and a name in a comment or a description for a list of the directors, board members and administrators to pick from (arrows move, Enter or Tab picks, Esc leaves what you typed), and a mention is drawn as their name, which opens their profile on the radio; yours is marked. @board, @director, @administrator and @moderator are at the top of that list and tell everybody on Tasks who holds the role. Whoever wrote a comment, or an administrator, can delete it, and it asks first. A task’s comments go when the task is deleted. A comment brought over from the task’s page in Notion says in Notion after its time, and is its writer’s to edit here like any other. A task’s Activity Under every task, each change made to it, newest first: who changed what from what to what, and when. A description’s change says only that it changed, and a comment only that somebody commented. ← Back to … Above every view you reached from another one in tasks, saying which it goes back to. It goes back one step, not to the list or the street, to where you were in that view, with the keyboard on the link you followed; your browser’s Back and Forward, and Alt or Cmd and ←, do the same. A task opened on its own has ← Back to the list there instead, and a form the task it changes. Save, Cancel and Delete take the place of the step they were pressed on rather than adding one after it, so Back never lands on a finished form or a deleted task. New task A name, then whatever else it needs. A task can be assigned only to somebody who can read tasks. The description takes Markdown, and Preview shows how it will look. Saving a change sends only what you changed, so somebody else changing another part at the same moment keeps theirs. Privacy has what tasks keep.

The office holds the people and organisations we are in touch with, our grant requests, and our cases (connection requests, volunteer applications and join requests), moved here from EspoCRM, and the team mailbox’s email with them, in the CB’s colours like tasks. Only directors, board members and administrators can open it, on a claimed username, and everything in it is encrypted where it is kept. Numbers are fine here: every list says how many match, and grant requests what they come to. Part What it does Dashboard The office at a glance, and the page it opens on, worked out from its records each time you open it: a few sentences on what came in this week against the week before, each pipeline’s open grant requests submitted this year against its cap of 100, open cases and tasks, EspoCRM’s four dashboard reports as charts, how many messages went out on the CB each day for the last month (a number for World, the rooms and the moderators’ rooms, and never whose), and, from the night the office started keeping them, lines of how many grant requests, cases and tasks were open each night. Under QuickBooks, once a director has pressed Connect QuickBooks and signed in at Intuit: the money that came in over the last 30 days, each day and the newest twelve, and this year’s income and expenses by month. The office reads the books late each evening, and Read the books now reads them at once; it never writes to them, and Disconnect takes its permission back. Under Givebutter: what was given in the last 30 days against the 30 before, the recurring plans and what they give a month, every month of the last year, the campaigns and what each has raised, and the newest gifts, with nobody who gave named. It is read late each evening, and Read Givebutter now reads it at once. Every bar says its number, a pipeline wears the same colour on every chart, and The numbers under each chart shows them as a table. Newest, at the top, has the grant requests and cases submitted last (or added last, for one with no day it was submitted), the tasks made last, and the forum topics posted to last, of the ones you may read, each saying its category and who posted last; each heading opens its whole list. Reports EspoCRM’s nine reports, by their names: Active Applications This Year, Open Grant Requests by Stage, Grant Requests This Year by Month, Grant Requests by Year, Grants Awarded by Year, Grantees (a year at a time), Open Collaboration Cases, and Collaboration Cases by Status and by Year. A request or case counts in the year it was submitted, an award in the year it was decided. Feed Grant requests and cases as cards, after Notion’s Feed view, the one added or changed last first, with Contacts as well if you tick them under Show. Each card says what it is, who added or changed it and when, its facts and who it is from, and its description or notes, the first few parts with More for the rest. A grant request or a case moves on there with Move to, and Open goes to its page. A card says how many comments it has and shows the latest two, and Comment writes one where the card stands; a comment puts its card first, as a change does. Twenty cards at a time, with Show more at the foot; what it shows is kept in the page’s address. Contacts Everybody, a hundred at a time, with Show more at the foot. Their name, email and phone, and when they were added; NO EMAIL and NO CALLS mark somebody who has asked. A heading sorts by that column, and again the other way round; names sort by last name, and an empty email or phone goes last. Find a contact Any part of a name, an email or a phone number, every word of it; a phone number matches by its digits, however it was written. The order of the list is kept in the page’s address, and a search is not, because the address goes into your browser’s history: it lasts while the page is open. A contact Their email and phone, which open your mail or your phone, saying if they have asked not to be emailed or called; who added them and when, and who changed them last; their notes; their grant requests and cases, with New grant request from them and New case from them; and their Emails with the team mailbox, newest first, each saying whether it went to them or came from them, with Write to them in Gmail, which opens Gmail’s compose window addressed to them. Edit, and Delete, which asks first. A contact brought over from EspoCRM and deleted here stays deleted when contacts are brought over again. Write to them in Gmail opens a new email to them in Gmail; choose one of the mailing templates under With a template and it opens with the subject and words filled in for them, ready to read and send, such as the membership invite. A template that needs a grant request they have not made says so, and Copy the email copies it for pasting. A template with {invite} in it (since 2026-10-23) waits for Make their invite, which makes them a CB invite that works once and runs out after thirty days and puts its link in the email; then the Gmail link opens. Each press makes a new one, and nothing writes down whom it was for. A join request has Write to them too, for its contact. Grant requests Our Mutual Aid and Creator Grants requests, after EspoCRM’s: each in its pipeline and at a stage of it (Received, Holding, Holding (No Updates), Agreement Sent, Granted, Denied), and the stage says whether it is open, granted or denied. The list opens on the open ones; filter by pipeline, stage and status, each choice saying how many it would show, find one by its name, its contact or its form entry, and sort by any column. The line above it says how many are shown and what they come to. The pipeline, stage, status and order are kept in the page’s address, a search is not. Rest the pointer on a grant request’s name, or land on it with the keyboard, and its preview shows beside it, after a moment: what happened to it last, the first parts of its description and its latest comments. Esc puts it away, and you can move the pointer onto it to read it. Nothing on it can be pressed; its own page has the whole of it. Grant board One pipeline’s stages as columns, after EspoCRM’s Kanban, each saying how many it holds and what they come to. Drag a card to another stage, or use its own Move to, which is how a keyboard, a screen reader or a phone moves it. Granted and Denied keep their cards folded until opened. A grant request Its pipeline, stage, amount, the days it was submitted and decided, its contact and its form entry, who added it and who changed it last, and its description. Move to changes its stage there and then; Edit changes anything; Delete asks first. Moving it to Granted or Denied sets the day it was decided, if none is given, and moving it back to an open stage clears it. New grant request A name, then whatever else there is. It links to a contact by the contact’s email, so the contact has to be in the office first; New grant request from them, on a contact’s page, fills it in. Moved to another pipeline, it starts at that pipeline’s first stage unless you pick one. Cases Connection requests, volunteer applications and join requests, after EspoCRM’s (a join request is the Join form’s entry, since 2026-10-22): each with its number, its type and a status (New, Assigned, Replied, Closed, Spam). The list opens on the open ones, newest number first; filter by type and status, find one by its number, name, contact or form entry, and sort by any column. Its Board has a column for each status, Closed and Spam folded; a card moves as a grant request’s does. A case’s page has Move to, Edit and Delete. Closing a case, here, sets the day it closed, if none is given, and opening it again clears it; a new case takes the next number, and a deleted case’s number is never given again. Rest the pointer on a case’s name, or land on it with the keyboard, and its preview shows beside it, after a moment: what happened to it last, the first parts of its description and its latest comments. Esc puts it away, and you can move the pointer onto it to read it. Nothing on it can be pressed; its own page has the whole of it. Mailing lists Since 2026-10-23, on a join request, under Mailing lists: which of our mailing lists they said yes to on the Join form, the Members Only list and the Monthly Newsletter. Add them to Givebutter’s lists sends Givebutter their name, their email address and those lists, and nothing else of their join request; it is never sent without that press. Givebutter finds somebody already there by their email and adds the lists without taking any away, and the join request then says which lists were sent and when. Taking somebody off a list is done in Givebutter. What goes is on the privacy page. Members page Since 2026-10-23, on a join request, under Members page, when they filled in that part of the Join form: the line they asked for on our Members page, their name or pseudonym, their website and their words, in boxes to tidy, with How it will look under them as stimpunks.org shows a line. Check the Members page reads the page and changes nothing: it says whose line this one goes after, and whether somebody by that name is on it already. Then Add them to the Members page writes that one line at the end of the page’s list, and nothing else of their join request; if the page changed since you checked, nothing is added and it says where the line goes now. The join request then says when they were added. Changing their line, or taking it off, is done on stimpunks.org, where WordPress keeps the page as it was before as a revision. What goes is on the privacy page. Organizations page Since 2026-10-23, on a join request, under Organizations page, when they filled in that part of the Join form: their organization’s entry for our Organizations page, in boxes to tidy. Type its name where the form did not ask it. Its ground is the colour its rounded box stands on. Check the Organizations page reads the page and changes nothing: it says whose entry this one goes after, picks the ground the page has used least lately, says whether the name or the website is on it already, and brings the logo they uploaded to look at, with its camera data taken off. Choose the logo or No logo, and say in What the logo shows what it shows, for anybody who cannot see it; How it will look shows the entry. Add it to the Organizations page copies that logo into stimpunks.org’s media library and writes the entry at the end of the page, and nothing else of their join request; if the page changed since you checked, nothing is added. Changing the entry, or taking it or its logo off, is done on stimpunks.org. What goes is on the privacy page. The member map Since 2026-10-22, the map of where our community lives, on the Community Center’s wall and on stimpunks.org, showing each place and how many of us are there, never a name. On a join request, under Member map, the place they gave on the Join form is filled in: Find it looks it up on OpenStreetMap, from our server, sending only those words; choose theirs, and Put it on the member map. A place near one already on the map joins it, and says so before you choose, unless you tick to keep it a place of its own. Take them off the map is there once they are on it, and deleting the join request takes them off too. The member map, at the top of Cases, lists every place with how many are there; the ones brought from our old Google map belong to no join request, so Take one off there takes one of those off a place when somebody asks. An email Who it is from and to, when it was sent, every contact it is filed on, its attachments by name (they stay in Gmail), and the whole of its text. Open the thread in Gmail opens it there, signed in as the team mailbox, which is the way to answer in the thread; Reply in Gmail opens a new email with the subject; Delete from the office, which asks first, takes it off every contact and leaves it in Gmail, and it is never filed again. Emails arrive by themselves, every ten minutes, from a script in the team mailbox; nobody files them by hand. Mailings An email from a template to everybody at one stage of a grant pipeline, one email to each person, sent from the team mailbox. The list says, for each mailing, its template and stage, who sent it and when, and how many have been sent, are waiting to go, Google would not send, or were stopped. Email everyone at a stage On the grant requests list, once it shows one pipeline and one stage, this opens a new mailing to that stage. New mailing Choose the pipeline, the stage and the template, and if you like a Submitted since day (This year fills in the first of January), because a stage holds everybody who ever reached it. Then Show every email: every email, filled in for its person, and everybody left out with the reason (no contact, no address, they asked not to be emailed, or, with a day, no submitted day), and how many earlier requests the day passed over. Send asks again, naming everybody it goes to. The team mailbox sends them within ten minutes, and each is filed on its contact once the mailbox sees it go. If the template or who is at the stage changes after you look, it asks you to look again. A mailing Its template’s words as they were, and each person with where their email is. Stop the rest takes back the emails not sent yet; once nothing is waiting, Delete this record deletes the office’s record of it and leaves the emails in Gmail. Templates A name, a subject and plain words, with fill-ins in braces: {first}, {last}, {name}, {grant}, {amount}, {pipeline}, {stage} and {submitted}. A fill-in the office does not know is refused when you save, so a misspelt one never goes out. Each template has a page of its own, with its words, Edit, Send it as a mailing, Delete and its comments. The Office label, in Gmail For somebody who wrote to the team mailbox and is not in the office yet: put the Office label on one of their emails, in Gmail on the web or on a phone, or have a Gmail filter put it on. Within ten minutes they are a contact, named as the email names them and added by the team mailbox, and the whole thread is on their page. For an email we started, whoever it was sent to is added; somebody already in the office is not added twice. Change their name in the office if the email had it wrong. Comments At the foot of every contact, grant request, case, mailing, template and filed email, as under a task in Tasks: the conversation about it, oldest first, and a box to add to it, with Preview; Ctrl or Cmd and Enter posts it. They are encrypted where they are kept, like everything in the office. A comment tells whoever added the record, anybody who commented on it before and anybody it @mentions, in their Notifications in Tasks, which is where to look for them; that notification says only what kind of record it is on, never its name, and Open it in the office opens it on the comment. @ and a name offers the people who can open the office, and the roles, and a mention is drawn as their name, which opens their profile; a description or notes tell nobody, so a name there stays words. Only whoever wrote a comment can edit it; they or an administrator can delete it, and it asks first. A record’s comments go when it is deleted. ← Back to … Above every view you reached from another one in the office, saying which it goes back to. It goes back one step, not to a list or the street, to where you were in that view, with the keyboard on the link you followed, and the contacts you had shown with Show more shown again; your browser’s Back and Forward, and Alt or Cmd and ←, do the same. A contact, grant request, case or email opened on its own has its list or its contact there instead, and a form what it changes. Save, Cancel, Send and Delete take the place of the step they were pressed on rather than adding one after it, so Back never lands on a finished form or something deleted. A search is still kept only while the page is open, so it is there when you go back. New contact A first or last name, then whatever else there is. A new contact with an email somebody already has is refused, saying whose, so nobody is added twice. The notes take Markdown, and Preview the notes shows how they will look. The first sheets went through the printer and cut cleanly, so the spacing stays as it is. Wide-Spread Chaos Gardens is open, east of the stile in Nature’s Contribution: food and flowers from a mix of seed thrown into the wind, on a clear windy day with everything in the garden leaning the same way. What chaos gardening is, and what it is not, in the words of a landscape specialist at Colorado State University Extension: a garden, not a restoration. The mix is half things to eat and half flowers, and the four noxious weeds Colorado State University Extension says to keep out of a seed mix are named and never in it. It gives food to the café in the old dairy and the honesty box, flowers and seed, and a bench in the middle with no paths to keep to. The Honesty Box is open on the street, a farm stand at the kerb lit by its own solar lamp, with the wool, hemp rope and cloth, pasteurised milk and cheese, eggs, meat and produce of the land past the campgrounds. Prices on the board, money in the box, and nobody watching. It is the one stall on the street with prices, because selling the land’s goods is the land’s half of the bargain with the street. Every item says what it costs and which place it came from, and the board is checked against what each place sends here. Never in the box: cannabis, which leaves the land through licensed dispensaries only, because a box nobody watches cannot ask anybody’s age; raw milk; and anything from the sanctuary.

The Dairy is open, behind All Together Now Farms: the farm’s old dairy is a café now, white glazed tile to the ceiling with the light going round and round it, and the pasteuriser still on the counter. All Together Now Farms is open, north-east of the stile: a mixed farm where trees, crops and animals share the same fields, lit by the sun going down on one side and the full moon coming up on the other, so everything on it is warm on one side and silver on the other. The five agroforestry practices in the USDA’s own words, and which the farm does: four of them, and the fifth says why not. 2026-10-05 — A Quiet Pint: a pub under the street, made like McAnally’s

A Quiet Pint is a new shopfront, at Ryan’s ask: a pub a few steps down from the street, made like McAnally’s in Jim Butcher’s Dresden Files. Thirteen tables, thirteen stools along a bar that meanders, thirteen carved columns, thirteen windows, thirteen mirrors and thirteen ceiling fans, as in the books, and no two of any of them alike. There is no television, no games machine and no jukebox, only a player piano. The only light is the street’s, through small windows at the level of the pavement, passed round the room by old mirrors, so it lands in patches, none the same shape, a little dimmer and a little green. Nobody lights a lamp and the stove is shut. Nothing in the pub moves, at any setting, the fans included. A table that fits you. The tables are all different heights, so the room has a plan of the floor and a list of every table in words, with boxes to tick for what you want: room under it for a wheelchair or your knees, a tall table, a low one with soft seats, your back to a wall, out of sight of the door, away from the bar, by the stove, in a patch of light or out of it. Every table can be reached from the door by a way at least 36 inches wide, and the room’s own tool walks the floor to make sure. Sit at a table, order from the bar, and look down to see your table. Where it parts from the books, and says so: a ramp beside the steps, as wide as they are; the ceiling still low, but the fans up between the beams; and your order fetched from the bar or brought to you, whichever you say, and nobody asks why. The measurements are the 2010 ADA Standards’, read on the Access Board’s page. Every pint comes alcohol-free first, in the same glass, at the same size, so nobody can tell from across the room which one anybody has. Ale at cellar temperature, never cold; lemonade with lemonade ice; a mushroom sandwich first and a steak sandwich after it, from the stove. Nothing has a price, and nobody has to order anything to sit down, which is our own Third Places page’s line. Butcher’s words are quoted, not retold: short passages, each naming its book and pages, held to a cap. 2026-09-23 — Lighter pictures, where that is measurably true

Fifty-six of the street’s JPEGs are WebP now, and the pictures on those pages weigh about 29% less — 2.4MB across the scans, prints, engravings, photographs and thumbnails. The biggest single waste went with it: the Pebble Board’s video thumbnails were stored 1280 pixels wide and are never drawn wider than 170, and they are 512 now, which still covers a phone screen at three times density. Twenty-four stayed JPEG, each for a reason written down. Every file was converted at the lowest quality that measured as faithful to its source, and swapped only if that saved at least a tenth. Most of Doré’s and Tenniel’s engravings did not clear that bar: fine hatching is the one thing lossy formats are worst at, and at the same fidelity WebP was no smaller than the JPEG, sometimes larger. Converting them anyway would have meant a heavier file or a softer engraving, chosen for the format’s sake. data/webp.json holds every decision and its numbers. The first attempt measured the wrong thing and was undone. It compared colour as well as detail, and WebP always stores colour at half resolution, as most JPEGs do — so on small, bright thumbnails it concluded no quality was good enough and left the oversized ones exactly as they were. It had deleted JPEGs under that rule, so everything went back to the last commit and ran again measuring detail, which is what the eye looks for. Nothing about the pages changed but the files. WebP goes into the same image tags, so no room’s layout moved; AVIF was often smaller still, but serving it safely means wrapping every picture in a new element, and at least one room’s layout depends on its images not being wrapped. The share cards and icons stay PNG, because link previews and home screens do not all read anything else. Every picture on the affected pages was loaded and checked afterwards, and the photographs still carry no location or device data. Turning 03 in The Outskirts is a venue. It earns that road rather than the campsite — crowds, volume and staying out late is exactly what the road is for. The light is thrown upward and nothing else on this street does that. Floods stand on the ground and point up the rock, so a face is brightest at its foot and goes dark towards the top, and there is nothing overhead at all. That is the exact inverse of Sithen one turning back, lit by a full moon from directly above, and of the Lagoon two turnings back, flat frontal light across water at eye level. Three rooms on one road, three directions of light, and vertical was the one nobody had taken. And what glows is not the lamp. The lichen fluoresces — it takes light you cannot see and gives back light you can — which is emission rather than reflection, and the third kind of transmitted light here after Swaying Sweetgrass (through grass) and The Feed (through a mask). The lamps are violet; what comes back is cyan-green. That green is the pair to watch: the Lagoon’s acid is a yellow-green one turning along the same road, and the two are far apart in blue on purpose. While the stage is dark, tuning is silent and nothing is fetched; once something is playing, tuning changes the picture. It was turning 03 in The Outskirts and it is a shopfront now. Ryan’s call, and the reasoning is about what each area is for rather than about decoration: the campgrounds are for people who want to be somewhat apart from each other, at peace in nature, with the street still in reach; the road out of town is for night revelry in crowds and for anybody who wants to be as far off as they can get. A covenstead is neither — a group that meets regularly wants a premises with a door on a street where people already are. Out there it was a dark kitchen lit by several lamps that did not match — the only room on the street lit by more than one source. On the street it is daylit, warm and domestic: one window, mid-afternoon, limewash, and the good china out. And the argument moved with it rather than being dropped. The device carrying several people who do not match, meeting anyway is now the china — nobody’s cup is anybody else’s cup. That is load bearing and is written into the section, the data file and the card’s alt text: if the crockery is ever made to match, the room has lost its subject and kept its wallpaper. Three pale rooms already existed and the light is what tells them apart. This is an interior with one window in the side of it. Its wall is warm and slightly pink where both the other daylit rooms are green-white — if this limewash ever cools towards green it has become the garden with furniture in it. A repaint leaves dead var() behind and nothing warns. Replacing the palette orphaned the job marker, which went on stroking a custom property that had stopped existing — and CSS drops an unknown one and paints nothing, so the kettle rendered with no line at all. Not an error anywhere, and check-contrast.py had nothing to say because the pair was gone rather than wrong. 2026-09-22 — Covenstead, and the only room here lit by more than one lamp

Turning 03 is open, and The Outskirts now has a road behind every board. Covenstead is a meeting place with the door shut and the kettle on: a greeting with the goodbye built into it, counsel that stayed counsel, a law the tradition argues about, and the practice of watching your own first thoughts. It is the only room on this street lit by more than one source, and that is the argument rendered as physics rather than decoration. Every other world here has exactly one light — a lamp, a screen, a fire, a moon, a headlight, the sun, or nothing. A covenstead is where a group meets, so everybody brought their own: one pool is candle-amber, one a cold bulb, one a rose shade, all at the same height because everybody is sitting down.
